title.zh: 卷108之二 禮志四之二
title.raw: 卷108之二 禮志四之二 Volume 108b Treatise 4: Rituals 2

sentences.zh: 世宗景明二年夏六月，祕書丞孫惠蔚上言：「臣聞國之大禮，莫崇明祀，祀之大者，莫過禘祫，所以嚴祖敬宗，追養繼孝，合享聖靈，審諦昭穆，遷毀有恒，制尊卑，有定體，誠慤著於中，百順應於外。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of summer in the second year of Jingming of Emperor Shizong, Secretariat Assistant Sun Huiwei submitted a memorial, saying: "Your subject has heard that among a state's great rites, none surpasses exalting and clarifying sacrificial worship; among sacrifices, none surpasses the ti and di; thereby to enforce reverence for ancestors and respect for the lineage, to pursue nurture and continue filial piety, to unite and enjoy the sacred spirits, to examine and fix the zhao and mu, to have constant rules for moving and destroying [tablets], to regulate honor and lowliness with a fixed form, sincerity and reverence manifest within, and the hundred obediences responding without.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of summer in the second year of Jingming under Emperor Xuanwu, Secretariat Assistant Sun Huiwei submitted a memorial: "I have heard that among a state's greatest ceremonies, none surpasses honoring and clarifying sacrifice, and among sacrifices none surpass the ti and di. By these rites one enforces reverence for ancestors and respect for the lineage, pursues nurture and continues filial piety, unites the sacred spirits in shared enjoyment, scrutinizes and fixes the zhao and mu arrangement, sets constant rules for moving and retiring spirit tablets, regulates rank and precedence in a fixed form, and makes sincerity and reverence manifest within so that the hundred forms of obedience respond without.

sentences.zh: 是以惟王創制，為建邦之典；

translations.literal: Therefore the sovereign king established institutions, making them the canon for founding a state;
translations.idiomatic: For this reason the sovereign kings of old established institutions as the canon for founding a state;

sentences.zh: 仲尼述定，為不刊之式。

translations.literal: Confucius recounted and fixed them, making them an immutable pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius recounted and fixed them into an immutable standard.

sentences.zh: 暨秦燔詩書，鴻籍泯滅。

translations.literal: When Qin burned the Odes and Documents, the great records perished.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qin burned the Odes and Documents, the great canonical texts were lost.

sentences.zh: 漢氏興求，拾綴遺篆，淹中之經，孔安所得，唯有卿大夫士饋食之篇。

translations.literal: When the Han arose they sought and gathered, patching together surviving texts; of the classics from Yanzhong, what Kong An obtained was only the sections on presentation of food by ministers, grandees, and officers.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han dynasty arose it sought and gathered what survived, patching together scattered texts; of the classics from Yanzhong that Kong An recovered, only the sections on presentation of food by ministers, grandees, and officers remained.

sentences.zh: 而天子諸侯享廟之祭、禘祫之禮盡亡。

translations.literal: Yet the sacrifices by which Son of Heaven and feudal lords enjoyed the ancestral temple, and the rites of ti and di, were wholly lost.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the temple sacrifices by which the Son of Heaven and feudal lords honored their ancestors, and the rites of ti and di, were entirely lost.

sentences.zh: 曲臺之記，戴氏所述，然多載尸灌之義，牲獻之數，而行事之法，備物之體，蔑有具焉。

translations.literal: The records of the Quetai, as set forth by the Dai clan, yet mostly record the meaning of presenting to the impersonator and pouring libations, and the numbers of victims offered, while the methods of conducting the rite and the forms of preparing the objects have none complete therein.
translations.idiomatic: The Quetai records set forth by the Dai clan mostly record the rites of presenting to the impersonator and pouring libations and the numbers of victims offered, but the methods of conducting the ceremony and the forms for preparing the ritual objects are nowhere complete.

sentences.zh: 今之取證，唯有王制一簡，公羊一冊。

translations.literal: For evidence today there is only one section of the Royal Regulations and one volume of the Gongyang [Commentary].
translations.idiomatic: For evidence today we have only one passage from the Royal Regulations and one volume of the Gongyang Commentary.

sentences.zh: 考此二書，以求厥旨。

translations.literal: Examining these two books, one seeks their purport.
translations.idiomatic: We must examine these two books to seek their purport.

sentences.zh: 自餘經傳，雖時有片記，至於取正，無可依攬。

translations.literal: Among the remaining classics and commentaries, although there are at times fragmentary records, as for taking them as authoritative standards, there is nothing on which to rely.
translations.idiomatic: Among the remaining classics and commentaries there are occasional fragmentary records, but for establishing authoritative standards there is nothing reliable to draw on.

sentences.zh: 是以兩漢淵儒、魏晉碩學，咸據斯文，以為朝典。

translations.literal: Therefore the profound scholars of the two Han and the eminent scholars of Wei and Jin all took this text as the court canon.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason the profound scholars of the two Han dynasties and the eminent scholars of Wei and Jin all took this text as the court canon.

sentences.zh: 然持論有深淺，及義有精浮，[1]故令傳記雖一，而探意乖舛。

translations.literal: Yet in holding to discussion there are depths and shallows, and in meaning there are refinements and superficialities,[1] so that although the transmitted records are one, in probing their intent they conflict.
translations.idiomatic: Yet their arguments differ in depth, and their interpretations in refinement or superficiality,[1] so that although the transmitted records are the same, their readings of intent conflict.

sentences.zh: 伏惟孝文皇帝，合德乾元，應靈誕載，玄思洞微，神心暢古，禮括商周，樂宣韶濩，六籍幽而重昭，五典淪而復顯，舉二經於和中，[2]一姬公於洛邑。

translations.literal: Your subject considers that Emperor Xiaowen united his virtue with the Qian origin, responded to the numinous and was born to his age, his profound thought penetrating the subtle, his divine mind fluent in antiquity, rites embracing Shang and Zhou, music spreading the Shao and Huo, the six classics dark yet again bright, the five canons sunk yet again manifest, raising the two classics in harmony,[2] unifying the Duke of Zhou in Luoyi.
translations.idiomatic: I consider that Emperor Wen united his virtue with Heaven's origin, responded to the numinous and came forth in his age, his profound thought penetrating the subtle and his inspired mind fluent in antiquity; his rites embraced Shang and Zhou, his music spread the Shao and Huo; the six classics, though obscured, shone forth again, and the five canons, though lost, reappeared; he raised the two classics in harmony[2] and unified the Duke of Zhou's legacy at Luoyi.

sentences.zh: 陛下叡哲淵凝，欽明道極，應必世之期，屬功成之會，繼文垂則，實惟下武。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is sagely and wise, profound and concentrated, revering the Way and reaching its utmost, responding to the term of a destined generation, belonging to the juncture when achievement is complete, continuing culture and handing down models—truly the lower Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is sagely and wise, profound and concentrated, revering the Way to its utmost, meeting the term of a destined generation and the juncture when great works are fulfilled, continuing culture and handing down models—truly the heir to King Wu.

sentences.zh: 而祫禘二殷，國之大事；

translations.literal: Yet the two Yin sacrifices of di and ti are great affairs of the state;
translations.idiomatic: Yet the two great Yin sacrifices, di and ti, are matters of the greatest state importance;

sentences.zh: 蒸嘗合享，朝之盛禮。

translations.literal: the zheng and chang with united enjoyment are the court's grand rites.
translations.idiomatic: and the zheng and chang sacrifices with united enjoyment are the court's greatest ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 此先皇之所留心，聖懷以之永慕。

translations.literal: These were what the late emperor kept in mind; the sage heart forever cherishes them.
translations.idiomatic: These were what the late emperor kept at heart, and Your Majesty's sacred mind cherishes them without end.

sentences.zh: 臣聞司宗初開，致禮清廟，敢竭愚管，輒陳所懷。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that the Director of Ancestral Worship has newly opened [rites], extending ceremony to the Pure Temple; I dare exhaust my foolish narrowness and forthwith set forth what I hold.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the Director of Ancestral Worship has newly opened the rites and extended ceremony to the Pure Temple; I dare offer my humble thoughts and set forth what I hold.

sentences.zh: 謹案王制曰：『天子犆礿、祫禘、祫嘗、祫烝。』

translations.literal: Respectfully examining the Royal Regulations, it says: "The Son of Heaven exclusively performs yue, di and ti, di and chang, di and zheng."
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully examining the Royal Regulations, it states: "The Son of Heaven exclusively performs the yue sacrifice, di and ti, di and chang, and di and zheng."

sentences.zh: 鄭玄曰『天子諸侯之喪畢，合先君之主於祖廟而祭之，謂之祫。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan says: "When mourning for the Son of Heaven or feudal lords is complete, combining the tablets of former lords in the ancestral temple and sacrificing to them is called di.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan says: "When mourning for the Son of Heaven or feudal lords is complete, combining the spirit tablets of former lords in the ancestral temple and sacrificing to them is called di.

sentences.zh: 後因以為常』，『魯禮，三年喪畢而祫於太祖，明年春禘於羣廟，自爾之後，五年而再殷祭，一祫一禘』。

translations.literal: Later it became constant." "In Lu ritual, when the three-year mourning is complete one performs di at the Grand Ancestor; the next spring one performs ti at all the temples; thereafter, every five years there are again two Yin sacrifices, one di and one ti."
translations.idiomatic: Later this became the regular practice." "In Lu ritual, when the three-year mourning is complete one performs di at the Grand Ancestor; the next spring one performs ti at all the temples; thereafter, every five years there are again two Yin sacrifices, one di and one ti."

sentences.zh: 春秋公羊魯文二年：『八月丁卯，大事于太廟。』

translations.literal: The Gongyang [Commentary] on the Spring and Autumn Annals, Duke Wen of Lu, year 2: "On the day dingmao of the eighth month, a great affair at the Grand Temple."
translations.idiomatic: The Gongyang Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals, Duke Wen of Lu, year 2: "On dingmao day of the eighth month, a great affair was held at the Grand Temple."

sentences.zh: 傳曰：『大事者何？

translations.literal: The transmission says: "What is the great affair?"
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: "What is the great affair?"

sentences.zh: 大祫也。

translations.literal: It is the great di.
translations.idiomatic: It is the great di.

sentences.zh: 大祫者何？

translations.literal: What is the great di?
translations.idiomatic: What is the great di?

sentences.zh: 合祭也。

translations.literal: It is a united sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: It is a united sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 毀廟之主，陳於太祖。

translations.literal: The tablets of temples that have been destroyed are displayed before the Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: The tablets of shrines that have been retired are displayed before the Grand Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 未毀廟之主，皆升，合食于太祖。

translations.literal: The tablets of temples not yet destroyed all ascend and share food at the Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: The tablets of shrines not yet retired all ascend and share the offering at the Grand Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 五年而再殷祭。』

translations.literal: Every five years there are again two Yin sacrifices."
translations.idiomatic: Every five years the two Yin sacrifices are performed again."

sentences.zh: 何休曰：『陳者，就陳列太祖前。

translations.literal: He Xiu says: "To display means to arrange in array before the Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: He Xiu says: "To display means to arrange them in array before the Grand Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 太祖東鄉，昭南鄉，穆北鄉，其餘孫從王父。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor faces east; zhao faces south; mu faces north; the rest of the descendants follow their royal fathers.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor faces east; zhao faces south; mu faces north; the remaining descendants follow their royal fathers.

sentences.zh: 父曰昭，子曰穆。』

translations.literal: The father is called zhao; the son is called mu."
translations.idiomatic: The father is called zhao; the son is called mu."

sentences.zh: 又曰：『殷，盛也，謂三年祫，五年禘。

translations.literal: He also says: "Yin means abundant; it refers to di in the third year and ti in the fifth year.
translations.idiomatic: He also says: "Yin means abundant; it refers to di in the third year and ti in the fifth year.

sentences.zh: 禘所以異於祫者，功臣皆祭也。

translations.literal: The reason ti differs from di is that meritorious ministers are all sacrificed to.
translations.idiomatic: Ti differs from di in that meritorious ministers are all included in the sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 祫猶合也，禘猶諦也，審諦無所遺失。』

translations.literal: Di means uniting; ti means examining; examining carefully, nothing is left out."
translations.idiomatic: Di means uniting; ti means examining; by examining carefully, nothing is left out."

sentences.zh: 察記傳之文，何、鄭祫禘之義，略可得聞。

translations.literal: Examining the text of the records and transmissions, the meaning of di and ti in He and Zheng can briefly be heard.
translations.idiomatic: Examining the transmitted records, the meaning of di and ti in He Xiu and Zheng Xuan can be grasped in outline.

sentences.zh: 然則三年喪畢，祫祭太祖，明年春祀，遍禘羣廟。

translations.literal: Thus when the three-year mourning is complete, di sacrifices at the Grand Ancestor; the next spring sacrifices extend ti through all the temples.
translations.idiomatic: Thus when the three-year mourning is complete, one performs di at the Grand Ancestor; the next spring one sacrifices and performs ti throughout all the temples.

sentences.zh: 此禮之正也，古之道也。

translations.literal: This is the correctness of the rite, the way of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: This is the correct form of the rite, the way of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 又案魏氏故事，魏明帝以景初三年正月崩，至五年正月，積二十五晦為大祥。

translations.literal: Further examining Wei precedents: Emperor Ming of Wei died in the first month of the third year of Jingchu; by the first month of the fifth year, accumulating twenty-five last days of months constituted the great auspicious [end of mourning].
translations.idiomatic: Further examining Wei precedents: Emperor Ming of Wei died in the first month of the third year of Jingchu; by the first month of the fifth year, twenty-five last days of the month had accumulated to mark the great auspicious end of mourning.

sentences.zh: [3]太常孔美、博士趙怡等以為禫在二十七月，到其年四月，依禮應祫。

translations.literal: [3] Director of Ceremonies Kong Mei, Academician Zhao Yi, and others held that the chan [sacred garment removal] falls in the twenty-seventh month; reaching the fourth month of that year, according to ritual one should perform di.
translations.idiomatic: [3] Director of Ceremonies Kong Mei, Academician Zhao Yi, and others held that the chan falls in the twenty-seventh month; when the fourth month of that year arrived, di should be performed according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍王肅、博士樂詳等以為禫在祥月，至其年二月，宜應祫祭。

translations.literal: Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Su, Academician Yue Xiang, and others held that the chan falls in the auspicious month; reaching the second month of that year, di sacrifice should suitably be performed.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Su, Academician Yue Xiang, and others held that the chan falls in the auspicious month; when the second month of that year arrived, di sacrifice should be performed.

sentences.zh: 雖孔王異議，六八殊制，至於喪畢之祫，明年之禘，其議一焉。

translations.literal: Although Kong and Wang differed in opinion and the sixth and eighth [months] had different regulations, as for di when mourning is complete and ti the next year, their discussions were one.
translations.idiomatic: Although Kong and Wang disagreed and the sixth- and eighth-month systems differed, on di when mourning is complete and ti the following year their views were the same.

sentences.zh: 陛下永惟孝思，因心即禮，取鄭捨王，禫終此晦，來月中旬，禮應大祫。

translations.literal: Your Majesty forever ponders filial thought, following the heart to enact ritual, taking Zheng and discarding Wang; the chan ends this last day of the month; in the middle of next month, ritual should have the great di.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty forever ponders filial devotion and follows the heart in enacting ritual, taking Zheng Xuan and setting aside Wang Su; the chan ends on this last day of the month, and in the middle of next month the great di should be performed according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 六室神祏，升食太祖。

translations.literal: The spirit tablets of the six chambers ascend to share food at the Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit tablets of the six chambers should ascend to share the offering at the Grand Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 明年春享，咸禘羣廟。

translations.literal: Next spring's enjoyment: ti throughout all the temples.
translations.idiomatic: Next spring's seasonal sacrifice should extend ti throughout all the temples.

sentences.zh: 自茲以後，五年為常。

translations.literal: From this thereafter, five years is the constant.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, every five years should be the regular practice.

sentences.zh: 又古之祭法，時祫並行，天子先祫後時，諸侯先時後祫。

translations.literal: Further, in ancient sacrificial law seasonal and di [rites] proceeded in parallel: the Son of Heaven first di then seasonal; feudal lords first seasonal then di.
translations.idiomatic: Further, in ancient sacrificial law seasonal sacrifices and di proceeded in parallel: the Son of Heaven performed di before the seasonal sacrifices, feudal lords the seasonal sacrifices before di.

sentences.zh: 此於古為當，在今則煩。

translations.literal: This was appropriate in antiquity; today it would be burdensome.
translations.idiomatic: This was appropriate in antiquity, but today it would be burdensome.

sentences.zh: 且禮有升降，事有文節，通時之制，聖人弗違。

translations.literal: Moreover ritual has ascent and descent; affairs have pattern and restraint; the regulation suited to the age—the sage does not violate it.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover ritual has its gradations and affairs their formal restraint; the regulation suited to the times is what the sage does not violate.

sentences.zh: 當祫之月，宜減時祭，以從要省。

translations.literal: In the month when di is performed, seasonal sacrifices should suitably be reduced, to follow essential economy.
translations.idiomatic: In the month when di is performed, seasonal sacrifices should be reduced to follow essential economy.

sentences.zh: 然大禮久廢，羣議或殊，以臣觀之，理在無怪。

translations.literal: Yet the great rite has long been abandoned; the multitude of discussions may differ—in your subject's view, there is reason not to wonder.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the great rite has long been abandoned and opinions may differ; in my view there is nothing strange in this.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 心制既終，二殷惟始，祫禘之正，實在於斯。

translations.literal: The heart's regulation is already ended; the two Yin [sacrifices] are only beginning; the correctness of di and ti truly lies in this.
translations.idiomatic: The heart's mourning regulation has ended and the two Yin sacrifices are only beginning; the true form of di and ti lies precisely here.

sentences.zh: 若停而闕之，唯行時祭，七聖不聞合享，百辟不覩盛事，何以宣昭令問，垂式後昆乎？

translations.literal: If one stops and omits it, performing only seasonal sacrifices, the seven sages would not hear united enjoyment, the hundred officials would not behold the grand affair—how could one proclaim and make bright the excellent reputation and hand down a model to later generations?
translations.idiomatic: If it is halted and omitted and only seasonal sacrifices are performed, the seven sages would not hear united enjoyment and the hundred officials would not behold the grand ceremony—how could one proclaim a shining reputation and hand down a model to later generations?

sentences.zh: 皇朝同等三代，治邁終古，而令徽典缺於昔人，鴻美慚於往志，此禮所不行，情所未許。

translations.literal: Our dynasty equals the Three Dynasties; its governance surpasses all antiquity—yet to let the splendid canon lack what former men had, and great beauty be shamed before past records—this the rite cannot permit; feeling cannot allow.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty equals the Three Dynasties and its governance surpasses all antiquity, yet to let a splendid canon fall short of what former men possessed and great beauty be shamed before past records—this the rite cannot permit and feeling cannot allow.

sentences.zh: 臣學不鈎深，思無經遠，徒閱章句，蔑爾無立。

translations.literal: Your subject's learning does not hook the profound; his thought has no classic reach—merely reading passages and clauses, negligibly without establishment.
translations.idiomatic: My learning does not reach the profound and my thought lacks classic breadth; I have merely read passages and clauses and have nothing established to my credit.

sentences.zh: 但飲澤聖時，銘恩天造，是以妄盡區區，冀有塵露。

translations.literal: Yet having drunk the bounty of the sage age and engraved gratitude for Heaven's making, therefore I presumptuously exhaust my paltriness, hoping there may be a speck of dew.
translations.idiomatic: Yet having received the bounty of this sage age and engraved gratitude for Heaven's gift, I presumptuously offer my paltry thoughts, hoping they may amount to a speck of dew.

sentences.zh: 所陳蒙允，請付禮官，集定儀注。」

translations.literal: What I have set forth, if granted approval, I request be handed to the ritual officials to assemble and fix the ceremonial regulations."
translations.idiomatic: If what I have set forth is approved, I request that it be handed to the ritual officials to assemble and fix the ceremonial regulations."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「禮貴循古，何必改作。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Ritual values following antiquity—why must one change and create?
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Ritual values following antiquity—why must we change and create anew?

sentences.zh: 且先聖久遵，綿代恒典，豈朕冲闇，所宜革之。

translations.literal: Moreover the former sages long observed it; generation after generation it is the constant canon—how could I, young and dim, be one to reform it?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the former sages long observed it as the constant canon of generation after generation—how could I, young and unlearned, be fit to reform it?

sentences.zh: 且禮祭之議，國之至重，先代碩儒，論或不一。

translations.literal: Moreover discussion of ritual sacrifice is of the utmost weight to the state; eminent scholars of former ages sometimes did not agree in discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover discussion of ritual sacrifice is of the utmost importance to the state, and eminent scholars of former ages did not always agree.

sentences.zh: 可付八坐、五省、太常、國子參定以聞。」

translations.literal: It may be handed to the Eight Seats, the Five Ministries, the Director of Ceremonies, and the Imperial University to deliberate jointly and report."
translations.idiomatic: Let it be handed to the Eight Seats, the Five Ministries, the Director of Ceremonies, and the Imperial University to deliberate jointly and report."

sentences.zh: 七月，侍中、錄尚書事、北海王詳等言：「奉旨集議，僉以為禘祫之設，前代彝典，惠蔚所陳，有允舊義。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Attendant-in-Ordinary and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing, Prince Xiang of Beihai, and others said: "Receiving the edict we assembled for discussion; all considered that the establishment of ti and di is the constant canon of former ages; what Huiwei set forth accords with old meaning.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, Attendant-in-Ordinary and Recorder of the Masters of Writing, Prince Xiang of Beihai, and others said: "Having received the edict we assembled for discussion; all agreed that the establishment of ti and di is the constant canon of former ages and that what Huiwei set forth accords with established meaning.

sentences.zh: 請依前剋敬享清宮，其求省時祭，理實宜爾。

translations.literal: We request that according to the previous schedule one respectfully enjoy [sacrifice] at the Pure Palace; as for the request to reduce seasonal sacrifices, in principle it truly should be so.
translations.idiomatic: We request that according to the previous schedule sacrifice be respectfully performed at the Pure Palace; as for the request to reduce seasonal sacrifices, that is indeed reasonable in principle.

sentences.zh: 但求之解注，下逼列國，兼時奠之敬，事難輒省。

translations.literal: Yet seeking its explanation and commentary presses down on the feudal states; combining seasonal presentation of respect—the affair is hard to reduce forthwith.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when one seeks its full explanation it presses down on all the feudal states, and combining the seasonal presentations of respect—the matter is hard to reduce immediately.

sentences.zh: 請移仲月，擇吉重聞。」

translations.literal: We request moving it to the intercalary month and choosing an auspicious day to report again."
translations.idiomatic: We request postponing it to the intercalary month and choosing an auspicious day to report again."

sentences.zh: 制可。

translations.literal: The regulation was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The regulation was approved.

sentences.zh: 十一月壬寅，改築圓丘於伊水之陽。

translations.literal: On the day renyin of the eleventh month, the Round Mound was rebuilt on the south bank of the Yi River.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin day of the eleventh month, the Round Mound altar was rebuilt on the south bank of the Yi River.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，仍有事焉。

translations.literal: On yimao, the affair was again performed.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao day, the ceremony was performed again.

sentences.zh: 延昌四年正月，世宗崩，肅宗即位。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year of Yanzhang, Emperor Shizong died and Emperor Suzong ascended.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year of Yanzhang, Emperor Xuanwu died and Emperor Xiaoming ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 三月甲子，尚書令、任城王澄奏，太常卿崔亮上言：「秋七月應祫祭于太祖，今世宗宣武皇帝主雖入廟，然烝嘗時祭，猶別寢室，至於殷祫，宜存古典。

translations.literal: On the day jiazi of the third month, the Master of Writing, Prince Cheng of Rencheng, memorialized; Director of Ceremonies Cui Liang submitted: "In the seventh month of autumn di sacrifice should be performed at the Grand Ancestor. Today the tablet of Emperor Shizong Xuanwu, though entered the temple, yet for zheng, chang, and seasonal sacrifices still has a separate chamber; as for the Yin di, the ancient canon should be preserved.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi day of the third month, Master of Writing Prince Cheng of Rencheng memorialized that Director of Ceremonies Cui Liang had submitted: "Di sacrifice should be performed at the Grand Ancestor in the seventh month of autumn. Although the tablet of Emperor Xuanwu has entered the temple, for zheng, chang, and seasonal sacrifices it still has a separate chamber; for the great Yin di, the ancient canon should be preserved.

sentences.zh: 案禮，三年喪畢，祫於太祖，明年春禘於羣廟。

translations.literal: Examining ritual: when the three-year mourning is complete, di at the Grand Ancestor; the next spring ti at all the temples.
translations.idiomatic: According to ritual, when the three-year mourning is complete one performs di at the Grand Ancestor, and the next spring ti at all the temples.

sentences.zh: 又案杜預亦云，卒哭而除，三年喪畢而禘。

translations.literal: Further examining Du Yu, he also says: at the end of wailing one removes [mourning garments]; when the three-year mourning is complete, ti.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu also says that mourning garments are removed at the end of wailing and ti is performed when the three-year mourning is complete.

sentences.zh: 魏武宣后以太和四年六月崩，其月既葬，除服即吉。

translations.literal: Empress Wu Xuan of Wei died in the sixth month of the fourth year of Taihe; that month she was already buried, mourning garments removed and auspicious rites immediately performed.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu Xuan of Wei died in the sixth month of the fourth year of Taihe; that same month she was buried, mourning garments were removed, and auspicious rites were immediately resumed.

sentences.zh: 四時行事，而猶未禘。

translations.literal: The four seasons' affairs proceeded, yet ti was still not performed.
translations.idiomatic: Seasonal rites proceeded through the four seasons, yet ti was still not performed.

sentences.zh: 王肅、韋誕並以為今除即吉，故特時祭。

translations.literal: Wang Su and Wei Dan both held that today removal [of mourning] immediately leads to auspicious rites, therefore only seasonal sacrifices specially.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su and Wei Dan both held that because mourning is removed and auspicious rites resumed immediately, only seasonal sacrifices are performed in the interim.

sentences.zh: 至於禘祫，宜存古禮。

translations.literal: As for ti and di, the ancient rites should be preserved.
translations.idiomatic: As for ti and di, the ancient rites should be preserved.

sentences.zh: 高堂隆亦如肅議，於是停不殷祭。

translations.literal: Gao Tanglong also followed Su's discussion; therefore they halted and did not perform Yin sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Tanglong also followed Wang Su's view, and so Yin sacrifices were halted.

sentences.zh: 仰尋太和二十三年四月一日，高祖孝文皇帝崩，其年十月祭廟，景明二年秋七月祫於太祖，三年春禘於羣廟。

translations.literal: Looking up and tracing the first day of the fourth month of the twenty-third year of Taihe, when the High Ancestor Emperor Xiaowen died—in that year the tenth month temple sacrifice; in the seventh month of autumn of the second year of Jingming di at the Grand Ancestor; in the third spring ti at all the temples.
translations.idiomatic: Looking back to the first day of the fourth month of the twenty-third year of Taihe, when the High Ancestor Emperor Wen died: temple sacrifice was performed that year in the tenth month; di at the Grand Ancestor in the seventh month of autumn of the second year of Jingming; ti at all the temples in the third spring.

sentences.zh: 亦三年乃祫。

translations.literal: Again, only after three years was di performed.
translations.idiomatic: Again, di was performed only after three years.

sentences.zh: 謹準古禮及晉魏之議，并景明故事，愚謂來秋七月，祫祭應停，宜待三年終乃後祫禘。」

translations.literal: Respectfully following ancient ritual and the discussions of Jin and Wei, together with the Jingming precedent, this fool considers that the di sacrifice coming autumn seventh month should be halted; one should wait until the three years are ended and only then perform di and ti."
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully following ancient ritual, the discussions of Jin and Wei, and the Jingming precedent, I consider that the di sacrifice planned for the seventh month of next autumn should be halted; one should wait until the three years of mourning are complete and only then perform di and ti."

sentences.zh: [5]詔曰：「太常援引古今，並有證據，可依請。」

translations.literal: [5] An edict said: "The Director of Ceremonies cites antiquity and the present, all with evidence; his request may be followed."
translations.idiomatic: [5] An edict said: "The Director of Ceremonies cites antiquity and the present with supporting evidence; his request may be followed."

sentences.zh: 熙平二年三月癸未，太常少卿元端上言：「謹案禮記祭法：『有虞氏禘黃帝而郊嚳，祖顓頊而宗堯。

translations.literal: On the day guiwei of the third month of the second year of Xiping, Vice Director of Ceremonies Yuan Duan submitted: "Respectfully examining the Record of Rites, 'Methods of Sacrifice': 'The Youyu clan performed ti to the Yellow Emperor and suburban sacrifice to Ku, took Zhuanxu as zu and Yao as zong.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei day of the third month of the second year of Xiping, Vice Director of Ceremonies Yuan Duan submitted: "Respectfully examining the Record of Rites, 'Methods of Sacrifice': 'The Youyu clan performed ti to the Yellow Emperor and suburban sacrifice to Ku, took Zhuanxu as zu and Yao as zong.

sentences.zh: 夏后氏亦禘黃帝而郊鯀，祖顓頊而宗禹。

translations.literal: The Xia also performed ti to the Yellow Emperor and suburban sacrifice to Gun, took Zhuanxu as zu and Yu as zong.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia likewise performed ti to the Yellow Emperor and suburban sacrifice to Gun, took Zhuanxu as zu and Yu as zong.

sentences.zh: 殷人禘嚳而郊冥，祖契而宗湯。

translations.literal: The Yin performed ti to Ku and suburban sacrifice to Ming, took Xie as zu and Tang as zong.
translations.idiomatic: The Yin performed ti to Ku and suburban sacrifice to Ming, took Xie as zu and Tang as zong.

sentences.zh: 周人禘嚳而郊稷，祖文王而宗武王。』

translations.literal: The Zhou performed ti to Ku and suburban sacrifice to Ji, took King Wen as zu and King Wu as zong.'
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou performed ti to Ku and suburban sacrifice to Ji, took King Wen as zu and King Wu as zong.'

sentences.zh: 鄭玄注云：[6]『禘郊祖宗，謂祭祀以配食也。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan's commentary says:[6] 'Ti, suburban, zu, and zong mean sacrifices with accompanying food offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan's commentary says:[6] 'Ti, suburban, zu, and zong refer to sacrifices with accompanying offerings.

sentences.zh: 有虞氏以上尚德，禘郊祖宗，配用有德者。

translations.literal: From the Youyu clan upward they valued virtue; for ti, suburban, zu, and zong they used the virtuous as accompanying offerings.
translations.idiomatic: From the Youyu clan upward they valued virtue and used the virtuous as accompanying offerings for ti, suburban, zu, and zong.

sentences.zh: 自夏以下，稍用其姓代之。』

translations.literal: From Xia downward they gradually used men of their own surnames in place.'
translations.idiomatic: From the Xia downward they gradually used men of their own lineage in place.'

sentences.zh: 是故周人以后稷為始祖，文武為二祧。

translations.literal: Therefore the Zhou took Hou Ji as founding ancestor and Wen and Wu as the two tiao.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the Zhou took Hou Ji as founding ancestor and Wen and Wu as the two tiao shrines.

sentences.zh: 訖於周世，配祭不毀。

translations.literal: Through the Zhou age, accompanying sacrifices were not destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the Zhou, accompanying sacrifices were never retired.

sentences.zh: 案禮，嚳雖無廟，配食禘祭。

translations.literal: Examining ritual: although Ku had no temple, he received accompanying food at ti sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: According to ritual, although Ku had no temple of his own, he received accompanying offerings at ti sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 謹詳聖朝以太祖道武皇帝配圓丘，道穆皇后劉氏配方澤；

translations.literal: Respectfully examining in detail: our sage dynasty takes the Grand Ancestor Emperor Daowu as accompanying offering at the Round Mound, and Empress Dowager Dao Mu, Lady Liu, at the Square Marsh;
translations.idiomatic: Examining in detail our sage dynasty: the Grand Ancestor Emperor Daowu accompanies sacrifice at the Round Mound, and Empress Dowager Dao Mu, Lady Liu, at the Square Marsh;

sentences.zh: 太宗明元皇帝配上帝，明密皇后杜氏配地祇；

translations.literal: the Founding Ancestor Emperor Mingyuan accompanies the Supreme Lord, and Empress Ming Mi, the Du clan, accompanies the Earth Spirits;
translations.idiomatic: the Founding Ancestor Emperor Mingyuan accompanies the Supreme Lord, and Empress Ming Mi of the Du clan accompanies the Earth Spirits;

sentences.zh: 又以顯祖獻文皇帝配雩祀。

translations.literal: further the Manifest Ancestor Emperor Xianwen accompanies the yu sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: and the Manifest Ancestor Emperor Xianwen accompanies the yu sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 太宗明元皇帝之廟既毀，上帝地祇，配祭有式。

translations.literal: The temple of the Founding Ancestor Emperor Mingyuan has already been destroyed; for the Supreme Lord and Earth Spirits, accompanying sacrifice has a pattern.
translations.idiomatic: The shrine of the Founding Ancestor Emperor Mingyuan has already been retired; for the Supreme Lord and Earth Spirits, accompanying sacrifice follows an established pattern.

sentences.zh: 國之大事，唯祀與戎，廟配事重，不敢專決，請召羣官集議以聞。」

translations.literal: The great affairs of the state are only sacrifice and war; temple accompanying offerings are weighty—I dare not decide alone and request summoning all officials to assemble for discussion and report."
translations.idiomatic: The great affairs of the state are sacrifice and war alone; temple accompanying offerings are weighty matters. I dare not decide alone and request that all officials be summoned to deliberate jointly and report."

sentences.zh: 靈太后令曰「依請」。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling ordered: "As requested."
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling ordered: "As requested."

sentences.zh: 於是太師、高陽王雍，太傅、領太尉公、清河王懌，太保、領司徒公、廣平王懷，司空公、領尚書令、任城王澄，侍中、中書監胡國珍，侍中、領著作郎崔光等議：「竊以尚德尊功，其來自昔，郊稷宗文，周之茂典。

translations.literal: Thereupon Grand Preceptor Prince Yong of Gaoyang, Grand Tutor and Concurrent Grand Commandant Prince Yi of Qinghe, Grand Guardian and Concurrent Minister of Education Prince Huai of Guangping, Minister of Works and Concurrent Master of Writing Prince Cheng of Rencheng, Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Palace Secretariat Hu Guozhen, Attendant-in-Ordinary and Concurrent Director of the Bureau of Compilation Cui Guang, and others discussed: "We consider that honoring virtue and respecting merit come from of old; suburban sacrifice to Ji and zong to Wen are the Zhou's flourishing canon.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Grand Preceptor Prince Yong of Gaoyang, Grand Tutor and Concurrent Grand Commandant Prince Yi of Qinghe, Grand Guardian and Concurrent Minister of Education Prince Huai of Guangping, Minister of Works and Concurrent Master of Writing Prince Cheng of Rencheng, Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Palace Secretariat Hu Guozhen, Attendant-in-Ordinary and Concurrent Director of the Bureau of Compilation Cui Guang, and others discussed: "We consider that honoring virtue and respecting merit come from antiquity; suburban sacrifice to Ji and zong to Wen are the Zhou's flourishing canon.

sentences.zh: 仰惟世祖太武皇帝以神武纂業，克清禍亂，德濟生民，功加四海，宜配南郊。

translations.literal: Looking up we consider that the Manifest Ancestor Emperor Taiwu, by divine martial prowess succeeding to the enterprise, was able to clear away calamity and disorder, his virtue succoring the living people, his merit reaching the four seas—he should accompany sacrifice at the southern suburban altar.
translations.idiomatic: We consider that the Manifest Ancestor Emperor Taiwu, by divine martial prowess succeeding to the enterprise, cleared away calamity and disorder, succored the living people, and extended his merit to the four seas—he should accompany sacrifice at the southern suburban altar.

sentences.zh: 高祖孝文皇帝大聖膺期，惟新魏道，刑措勝殘，功同天地，宜配明堂。」

translations.literal: The High Ancestor Emperor Xiaowen, great sage receiving the mandate, alone renewed the Wei Way, punishments set aside surpassing remnant mercy, merit equal to Heaven and Earth—he should accompany sacrifice at the Bright Hall."
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor Emperor Wen, great sage receiving the mandate, alone renewed the Wei Way, set punishments aside in a reign surpassing remnant mercy, and achieved merit equal to Heaven and Earth—he should accompany sacrifice at the Bright Hall."

sentences.zh: 令曰：「依議施行。」

translations.literal: An edict stated: "Carry out according to the discussion."
translations.idiomatic: An edict stated: "Carry out according to the discussion."

sentences.zh: 七月戊辰，侍中、領軍將軍、江陽王繼表言：「臣功緦之內，太祖道武皇帝之後，於臣始是曾孫。

translations.literal: On the wuchen day of the seventh month, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Commander-in-Chief, Prince Ji of Jiangyang submitted a memorial, saying: "Within the scope of merit and the utmost-fine mourning grade, as descendant of the Grand Ancestor Emperor Daowu, I am only now a great-grandson.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuchen day of the seventh month, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Commander-in-Chief, Prince Ji of Jiangyang submitted a memorial: "Within the royal clan's utmost-fine mourning degree, as a descendant of the Grand Ancestor Emperor Daowu, I am only a great-grandson.

sentences.zh: 然道武皇帝傳業無窮，四祖三宗，功德最重，配天郊祀，百世不遷。

translations.literal: Yet Emperor Daowu transmitted the enterprise without end; the four ancestors and three zong have the weightiest merit and virtue, accompanying Heaven at suburban sacrifice, not moved for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Emperor Daowu transmitted the enterprise without end; the four ancestors and three zong bear the weightiest merit and virtue, accompany Heaven at suburban sacrifice, and are not moved for a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 而曾玄之孫，烝嘗之薦，不預拜於廟庭；

translations.literal: Yet great-great-grandsons and great-grandsons, at the seasonal offerings, do not participate in bowing in the temple courtyard;
translations.idiomatic: Yet great-great-grandsons and great-grandsons do not participate in bowing in the temple courtyard at the seasonal offerings;

sentences.zh: 霜露之感，闕陪奠於階席。

translations.literal: at the sentiment of frost and dew, they lack accompaniment in setting out offerings on the steps.
translations.idiomatic: and at the sentiment of frost and dew they are absent from accompanying offerings on the steps.

sentences.zh: 今七廟之後，非直隔歸胙之靈；

translations.literal: Now descendants of the seven temples are not merely separated from receiving sacrificial flesh;
translations.idiomatic: Now descendants of the seven temples are not merely cut off from receiving sacrificial flesh;

sentences.zh: 五服之孫，亦不霑出身之敍。

translations.literal: descendants within five degrees of mourning also do not receive ranking in birth-order precedence.
translations.idiomatic: descendants within five degrees of mourning also receive no birth-order ranking in precedence.

sentences.zh: 校之墳史則不然，驗之人情則未允。

translations.literal: Compared with canonical histories it is not so; tested against human sentiment it is not acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with canonical histories this is not so; tested against human sentiment it is unacceptable.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 禮云，祖遷於上，宗易於下。

translations.literal: The Rites say: zu move upward; zong shift downward.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites say: zu move upward; zong shift downward.

sentences.zh: 臣曾祖是帝，世數未遷，便疏同庶族，而孫不預祭。

translations.literal: My great-grandfather was an emperor; generations have not yet shifted, yet we are treated distant as the common clans, and as grandsons we do not participate in sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: My great-grandfather was an emperor; the generations have not yet shifted, yet we are treated as distant as common clans, and as grandsons we do not participate in sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 斯之為屈，今古罕有。

translations.literal: Such constriction is rare in past and present.
translations.idiomatic: Such an injustice is rare in past and present.

sentences.zh: 昔堯敦九族，周隆本枝，故能磐石維城，禦侮於外。

translations.literal: In antiquity Yao enriched the nine kin, Zhou elevated the root branch, and thus were able to be bedrock securing the wall and repel insult from without.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Yao enriched the nine kin, and Zhou elevated the root branch, and thus they were bedrock securing the realm and repelled insult from without.

sentences.zh: 今臣之所親，生見隔棄，豈所以楨幹根本，隆建公族者也。

translations.literal: Now those I am close to, in life see themselves cast off—how is this the means to be pillars and trunk for the root, to elevate and establish the ducal clan?
translations.idiomatic: Now those close to me are cast off in life—how is this the way to be pillars and trunk for the root and to elevate and establish the ducal clan?

sentences.zh: 伏見高祖孝文皇帝著令銓衡，取曾祖之服，以為資蔭，至今行之，相傳不絕。

translations.literal: I have seen that Emperor Xiaowen established regulations in weighing and balance, taking great-grandfather's mourning grade as basis for inheritance privilege, practiced to this day without break in transmission.
translations.idiomatic: I have seen that Emperor Wen established regulations in weighing and balance, taking the great-grandfather mourning grade as the basis for inheritance privilege—a practice carried on to this day without interruption.

sentences.zh: 而況曾祖為帝，而不見錄。

translations.literal: How much more when one's great-grandfather was emperor and is not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: How much more when one's great-grandfather was an emperor and is not recorded in temple rites.

sentences.zh: 伏願天鑒，有以照臨，令皇恩洽穆，宗人咸敍。

translations.literal: I wish Heaven's mirror to illuminate, making imperial grace harmonious, all lineage kin accorded ranking.
translations.idiomatic: I pray that Heaven's mirror may illuminate this, that imperial grace may be harmonious, and that all lineage kin may receive their proper ranking.

sentences.zh: 請付外博議，永為定準。」

translations.literal: I request referral for broad external discussion, to be the permanent standard."
translations.idiomatic: I request that this be referred for broad external discussion and made the permanent standard."

sentences.zh: 靈太后令曰：「付八座集禮官議定以聞。」

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling ordered: "Refer to the Eight Dignitaries to assemble ritual officers for discussion and report."
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling ordered: "Refer this to the Eight Dignitaries to assemble ritual officers for deliberation and report."

sentences.zh: 四門小學博士王僧奇等議：「案孝經曰：『郊祀后稷以配天，宗祀文王於明堂，以配上帝。』

translations.literal: Doctor Wang Siqi of the Four Gates Elementary School and others discussed: "Examining the Classic of Filial Piety, it says: 'Suburban sacrifice to Hou Ji to accompany Heaven; zong sacrifice to King Wen at the Bright Hall to accompany the Supreme Lord.
translations.idiomatic: Doctor Wang Siqi of the Four Gates Elementary School and others argued: "The Classic of Filial Piety says: 'At suburban sacrifice Hou Ji accompanies Heaven; at zong sacrifice King Wen is honored in the Bright Hall to accompany the Supreme Lord.

sentences.zh: 然則太祖不遷者，尊王業之初基，二祧不毀者，旌不朽之洪烈。

translations.literal: Thus the Grand Ancestor not moved honors the founding base of kingship; the two tiao not destroyed mark imperishable great magnificence.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Grand Ancestor, not moved, honors the founding base of kingship; the two tiao, not destroyed, mark imperishable great magnificence.

sentences.zh: 其旁枝遠胄，豈得同四廟之親哉？

translations.literal: How can collateral branches and distant descendants be the same kin as the four temples?
translations.idiomatic: How can collateral branches and distant descendants share the same kinship as the four temples?

sentences.zh: 故禮記婚義曰：『古者婦人先嫁三月，祖廟未毀，教於公宮。

translations.literal: Therefore the Record of Rites, Marriage Meaning, says: "In antiquity when a woman was betrothed three months in advance, if the zu temple was not yet destroyed, she was taught in the duke's palace.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the Record of Rites, Marriage Meaning, says: "In antiquity, when a woman was betrothed three months in advance, if the zu temple had not yet been retired, she was instructed in the duke's palace.

sentences.zh: 祖廟既毀，教于宗室。』

translations.literal: When the zu temple was destroyed, she was taught in the lineage chamber."
translations.idiomatic: When the zu temple had been retired, she was instructed in the lineage chamber."

sentences.zh: 又文王世子曰：『五廟之孫，祖廟未毀，雖庶人冠娶必告，死必赴，不忘親也。

translations.literal: Further the Son of King Wen says: "Grandsons of the five temples—while the zu temple is not destroyed, even as commoners at capping and marriage they must announce, at death they must report—not forgetting kin."
translations.idiomatic: Further, the Son of King Wen says: "Grandsons of the five temples—while the zu temple is not retired, even as commoners they must announce capping and marriage and report death, never forgetting kin."

sentences.zh: 親未絕而列於庶人，賤無能也。』

translations.literal: Kinship not yet ended yet listed as commoners—degrading their inability."
translations.idiomatic: Kinship not yet ended yet they are ranked as commoners—this degrades those who lack standing."

sentences.zh: 鄭注云：『赴告於君也。

translations.literal: Zheng's commentary says: "Reporting is to the lord."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng's commentary says: "Reporting is to the lord."

sentences.zh: 實四廟言五者，容顯考為始封君子故也。』

translations.literal: To speak of five while actually four temples accommodates the case where the illustrious father was the first enfeoffed gentleman."
translations.idiomatic: To speak of five temples while there are actually four accommodates the case where the illustrious father was the first enfeoffed gentleman."

sentences.zh: [7]鄭君別其四廟，理協二祭。

translations.literal: [7]Master Zheng distinguished the four temples, the reasoning coordinating the two sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: [7]Master Zheng distinguished the four temples, and his reasoning coordinates the two sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 而四廟者，在當世服屬之內，可以與於子孫之位，若廟毀服盡，豈得同於此例乎？

translations.literal: The four temples are within mourning kinship of the present generation; one may enter the status of descendant—if temples are destroyed and mourning exhausted, how can one be the same as this precedent?
translations.idiomatic: The four temples fall within the present generation's mourning kinship, and one may hold the status of descendant there—but if temples are retired and mourning exhausted, how can one be treated the same under this precedent?

sentences.zh: 敢竭愚昧，請以四廟為斷。」

translations.literal: I dare exhaust my ignorance and ask to take the four temples as the boundary."
translations.idiomatic: I dare offer this humble view and ask that the four temples be taken as the boundary."

sentences.zh: 國子博士李琰之議：「案祭統曰：『有事於太廟，羣昭羣穆咸在。』

translations.literal: Doctor Li Yanzhi of the National University discussed: "Examining the Sacrificial Summary, it says: 'When there is business at the Grand Temple, all zhao and all mu are present.
translations.idiomatic: Doctor Li Yanzhi of the National University argued: "The Sacrificial Summary says: 'When there is business at the Grand Temple, all zhao and all mu are present.

sentences.zh: 鄭氏注：『昭穆咸在，謂同宗父子皆來。』

translations.literal: Zheng's commentary: 'All zhao and mu present' means fathers and sons of the same zong all come."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng's commentary states: 'All zhao and mu present' means fathers and sons of the same zong all attend."

sentences.zh: 古禮之制，如是其廣，而當今儀注，唯限親廟四，愚竊疑矣。

translations.literal: The ancient rite's design is so broad, yet present-day ceremony and statutes limit only to four close temples—I privately doubt it.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient rite was designed so broadly, yet present-day ceremony and statutes limit participation to four close temples—I privately find this doubtful.

sentences.zh: 何以明之？

translations.literal: How is this made clear?
translations.idiomatic: How may this be clarified?

sentences.zh: 設使世祖之子男於今存者，既身是戚蕃，號為重子，可得賓於門外，不預碑鼎之事哉？

translations.literal: Suppose sons of the Manifest Ancestor who survive today—they are imperial princes and dukes, styled important sons—could they be guests outside the gate and not participate in stele and tripod affairs?
translations.idiomatic: Suppose sons of the Manifest Ancestor who survive today—they are imperial princes and dukes, styled important sons—could they be mere guests outside the gate and excluded from stele and tripod rites?

sentences.zh: 又因宜變法，禮有其說。

translations.literal: Further, adapting law to circumstances—the Rites have a doctrine on this.
translations.idiomatic: Further, adapting ritual to circumstances—the Rites themselves provide doctrine for this.

sentences.zh: 記言：『五廟之孫，祖廟未毀，為庶人，冠娶必告，死必赴。』

translations.literal: The Record says: "Grandsons of the five temples—while the zu temple is not destroyed, though commoners, at capping and marriage they must announce, at death they must report."
translations.idiomatic: The Record says: "Grandsons of the five temples—while the zu temple is not retired, though they be commoners, they must announce capping and marriage and report death."

sentences.zh: 注曰：『實四廟而言五者，容顯考始封之君子。』

translations.literal: The comment says: "To speak of five while actually four temples accommodates the illustrious father as first enfeoffed gentleman."
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: "To speak of five temples while there are actually four accommodates the illustrious father as the first enfeoffed gentleman."

sentences.zh: 今因太祖之廟在，仍通其曾玄侍祠，與彼古記，甚相符會。

translations.literal: Now because the Grand Ancestor's temple still stands, we still extend great-great-grandsons and great-grandsons to attend sacrifice—this accords very well with that ancient record.
translations.idiomatic: Now, because the Grand Ancestor's temple still stands, we still extend great-great-grandsons and great-grandsons to attend sacrifice—this accords very well with that ancient record.

sentences.zh: 且國家議親之律，指取天子之玄孫，乃不旁準於時后。

translations.literal: Moreover the state's law on deliberating kin takes specifically the Son of Heaven's fourth-generation descendants, and does not extend sideways to contemporaneous empresses.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the state's law on deliberating kin takes specifically the Son of Heaven's fourth-generation descendants and does not extend sideways to contemporaneous empresses.

sentences.zh: 至於助祭，必謂與世主相倫，將難均一。

translations.literal: As for assisting at sacrifice, it must mean parity with the reigning lord's generation—it will be hard to make uniform.
translations.idiomatic: As for assisting at sacrifice, it must mean parity with the reigning lord's generation—and that will be hard to make uniform.

sentences.zh: 壽有短長，世有延促，終當何時可得齊同。

translations.literal: Life has brevity and length, generations have prolongation and shortening—ultimately when can there be uniformity?
translations.idiomatic: Life has brevity and length, and generations have prolongation and shortening—ultimately, when can there be uniformity?

sentences.zh: 謂宜入廟之制，率從議親之條；

translations.literal: I say the rule for entering temples should generally follow the kin-deliberation articles;
translations.idiomatic: I propose that the rule for entering temples should generally follow the kin-deliberation articles;

sentences.zh: 祖祧之裔，各聽盡其玄孫。

translations.literal: descendants of zu and tiao should each be allowed through to their fourth-generation descendants.
translations.idiomatic: and descendants of zu and tiao should each be allowed through to their fourth-generation descendants.

sentences.zh: 使得駿奔堂壇，肅承禘礿，則情理差通。

translations.literal: enabling them to rush to the hall and altar, solemnly to receive ti and yue—then sentiment and principle would largely accord.
translations.idiomatic: This would enable them to rush to the hall and altar and solemnly receive the ti and yue—then sentiment and principle would largely accord.

sentences.zh: 不宜復各為例，令事事舛駁。」

translations.literal: One should not again make separate precedents for each matter, making everything contradictory."
translations.idiomatic: One should not again make separate precedents for each case and leave everything contradictory."

sentences.zh: 侍中、司空公、領尚書令、任城王澄，侍中、尚書左僕射元暉奏：「臣等參量琰之等議，雖為始封君子，又祭統曰：『有事於太廟，羣昭羣穆咸在，而不失其倫。』

translations.literal: Attendant-in-Ordinary, Minister of Works, Concurrent Master of Writing Prince Cheng of Rencheng, and Attendant-in-Ordinary, Left Vice Minister of the Master of Writing Yuan Hui submitted: "We weighed Yan Zhi's discussion—although it concerns a first enfeoffed gentleman, the Sacrificial Summary also says: 'When there is business at the Grand Temple, all zhao and all mu are present, without disrupting their order.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-Ordinary, Minister of Works, Concurrent Master of Writing Prince Cheng of Rencheng, and Attendant-in-Ordinary, Left Vice Minister of the Master of Writing Yuan Hui submitted: "We weighed Yan Zhi's argument—although it concerns a first enfeoffed gentleman, the Sacrificial Summary also says: 'When there is business at the Grand Temple, all zhao and all mu are present, without disrupting their order.

sentences.zh: 鄭注云昭穆，謂同宗父子皆來也。

translations.literal: Zheng's commentary on zhao and mu means fathers and sons of the same zong all come.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng's commentary on zhao and mu means fathers and sons of the same zong all attend.

sentences.zh: 言未毀及同宗，則共四廟之辭。

translations.literal: Speaking of 'not yet destroyed' and 'same zong' is the wording of sharing four temples.
translations.idiomatic: Speaking of 'not yet retired' and 'same zong' is the wording of sharing four temples.

sentences.zh: 云未絕與父子，明崇五屬之稱。

translations.literal: Speaking of 'not yet ended' with fathers and sons clarifies esteem for the designation of five degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Speaking of kin 'not yet ended' between fathers and sons clarifies esteem for the designation of five degrees.

sentences.zh: 天子諸侯，繼立無殊，吉凶之赴，同止四廟。

translations.literal: Son of Heaven and feudal lords, succession without difference—auspicious and inauspicious reporting alike stops at four temples.
translations.idiomatic: For the Son of Heaven and feudal lords alike, succession is without difference—auspicious and inauspicious reporting alike stops at four temples.

sentences.zh: 祖祧雖存，親級彌遠，告赴拜薦，典記無文。

translations.literal: Though zu and tiao remain, kin degree grows distant—announcement, reporting, bowing, offering: the canonical records have no text.
translations.idiomatic: Though zu and tiao remain, kinship grows more distant—announcement, reporting, bowing, and offering: the canonical records have no provision.

sentences.zh: 斯由祖遷於上，見仁親之義疏；

translations.literal: This is because zu move upward, showing the meaning of humane kin grows sparse;
translations.idiomatic: This is because zu move upward, showing that humane kinship grows sparse;

sentences.zh: 宗易於下，著五服之恩斷。

translations.literal: zong shift downward, marking the severance of five-degree mourning grace.
translations.idiomatic: and zong shift downward, marking the severance of five-degree mourning grace.

sentences.zh: 江陽之於今帝也，計親而枝宗三易，數世則廟應四遷，吉凶尚不告聞，拜薦寧容輒預。

translations.literal: For Jiangyang toward the present emperor, reckoning kin and branches the zong has shifted three times; several generations and temples should shift four times—even auspicious and inauspicious are not announced, how can bowing and offering be rashly permitted?
translations.idiomatic: For Jiangyang in relation to the present emperor, reckoning kin and branches the zong has shifted three times; after several generations the temples should have shifted four times—even auspicious and inauspicious matters are not announced; how can bowing and offering be rashly permitted?

sentences.zh: 高祖孝文皇帝聖德玄覽，師古立政，陪拜止於四廟，哀恤斷自緦宗。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen's sagely virtue and profound vision, taking antiquity as teacher to establish government—accompanying bowing stopped at four temples, mourning compassion cut off from the utmost-fine zong.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen's sagely virtue and profound vision, taking antiquity as teacher in establishing government, limited accompanying bowing to four temples and cut mourning compassion off at the utmost-fine zong.

sentences.zh: 即之人情，冥然符一；

translations.literal: As for human sentiment, it obscurely matches;
translations.idiomatic: As for human sentiment, it obscurely accords;

sentences.zh: 推之禮典，事在難違。

translations.literal: pushed against the ritual canon, the matter is hard to disobey.
translations.idiomatic: and pushed against the ritual canon, the matter is hard to disobey.

sentences.zh: 此所謂明王相沿，今古不革者也。」

translations.literal: This is what is called enlightened kings succeeding one another, past and present unchanging."
translations.idiomatic: This is what is called enlightened kings succeeding one another, unchanging from past to present."

sentences.zh: 太常少卿元端議：「禮記祭法云：王立七廟，曰考廟，曰王考廟，曰皇考廟，曰顯考廟，曰祖考廟，遠廟為祧，有二祧。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Grand Ritual Office Yuan Duan discussed: "The Record of Rites, Sacrificial Law, says: the king establishes seven temples—the Father temple, the Royal Father temple, the Imperial Father temple, the Illustrious Father temple, the Ancestor Father temple; distant temples become tiao, and there are two tiao.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Grand Ritual Office Yuan Duan argued: "The Record of Rites, Sacrificial Law, says that the king establishes seven temples—the Father temple, the Royal Father temple, the Imperial Father temple, the Illustrious Father temple, the Ancestor Father temple; distant temples become tiao, and there are two tiao.

sentences.zh: 而祖考以功重不遷，二祧以盛德不毀。

translations.literal: The Ancestor Father because of meritorious weight is not moved; the two tiao because of abundant virtue are not destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The Ancestor Father, because of meritorious weight, is not moved; the two tiao, because of abundant virtue, are not destroyed.

sentences.zh: 迭遷之義，其在四廟也。

translations.literal: The meaning of successive shifting lies in the four temples.
translations.idiomatic: The meaning of successive shifting lies in the four temples.

sentences.zh: 祭統云：祭有十倫之義，六曰見親疏之殺焉。

translations.literal: The Sacrificial Summary says sacrifice has the meaning of ten orders of relationship; the sixth is seeing the gradations of kin near and far.
translations.idiomatic: The Sacrificial Summary says sacrifice embodies ten orders of relationship; the sixth is seeing the gradations of kin near and far.

sentences.zh: 『夫祭有昭穆，昭穆者所以別父子遠近、長幼親疏之序，而無亂也』，是故有倫。

translations.literal: "Sacrifice has zhao and mu—zhao and mu are what distinguish father-son distance and nearness, senior and junior kin order, without disorder"—therefore there is order.
translations.idiomatic: "Sacrifice has zhao and mu—zhao and mu distinguish father-son distance and nearness and senior and junior kin order without disorder"—therefore there is order.

sentences.zh: 注云：『昭穆咸在，同宗父子皆來。』

translations.literal: The commentary says: "All zhao and mu present—fathers and sons of the same zong all come."
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: "All zhao and mu present—fathers and sons of the same zong all attend."

sentences.zh: 指謂當廟父子為羣，不繫於昭穆也。

translations.literal: This means fathers and sons of the current temple form a cluster, not bound to zhao and mu seating.
translations.idiomatic: This means fathers and sons of the current temple form a cluster, not bound to zhao and mu seating.

sentences.zh: 若一公十子，便為羣公子，豈待數公而立稱乎？

translations.literal: If one duke has ten sons, they are at once a cluster of duke's sons—must one wait for several dukes to establish the designation?
translations.idiomatic: If one duke has ten sons, they are at once a cluster of the duke's sons—must one wait for several dukes before the designation applies?

sentences.zh: 文王世子云『五廟之孫，祖廟未毀』，雖為有所援引，然與朝議不同。

translations.literal: The Son of King Wen says "grandsons of the five temples, zu temple not destroyed"—although there is some citation, it differs from the court discussion.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of King Wen says "grandsons of the five temples, zu temple not retired"—although there is some citation, it differs from the court discussion.

sentences.zh: 如依其議，匪直太祖曾玄，諸廟子孫，悉應預列。

translations.literal: If we follow that discussion, not only the Grand Ancestor's great-great-grandsons and great-grandsons—all temples' descendants should all be listed.
translations.idiomatic: If we follow that argument, not only the Grand Ancestor's great-great-grandsons and great-grandsons—all temples' descendants would have to be listed.

sentences.zh: 既無正據，竊謂太廣。

translations.literal: Having no proper evidence, I privately deem it too broad.
translations.idiomatic: Lacking proper evidence, I privately deem it too broad.

sentences.zh: 臣等愚見，請同僧奇等議。」

translations.literal: Our humble view: please agree with Sengqi and others' discussion."
translations.idiomatic: Our humble view is that we should agree with Sengqi and others' argument."

sentences.zh: 靈太后令曰：「議親律注云：『非唯當世之屬籍，歷謂先帝之五世。』

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling ordered: "The commentary on the kin-deliberation law says: 'Not only the present generation's registered kin—historically it means the former emperor's fifth generation.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling ordered: "The commentary on the kin-deliberation law says: 'Not only the present generation's registered kin—historically it means the former emperor's fifth generation.

sentences.zh: 此乃明親親之義篤，骨肉之恩重。

translations.literal: This clarifies the depth of kin-loving meaning, the weight of bone-and-flesh grace.
translations.idiomatic: This clarifies the depth of kin-loving meaning and the weight of bone-and-flesh grace.

sentences.zh: 尚書以遠及諸孫，太廣致疑。

translations.literal: The Master of Writing because it extends far to all grandsons—too broad and raises doubt.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Writing held that extending so far to all grandsons was too broad and raised doubt.

sentences.zh: 百僚助祭，可得言狹也！

translations.literal: That many officials assist sacrifice—can it be called narrow!
translations.idiomatic: That many officials assist at sacrifice—can that be called narrow!

sentences.zh: 祖廟未毀，曾玄不預壇堂之敬，便是宗人之昵，反外於附庸，王族之近，更疏於羣辟。

translations.literal: While the zu temple is not destroyed, great-great-grandsons and great-grandsons not participating in hall and altar reverence—then lineage kin are intimate yet cast outside feudatory attachment, and the royal clan's nearness is more distant than the host of ministers.
translations.idiomatic: While the zu temple is not retired, great-great-grandsons and great-grandsons excluded from hall and altar reverence means that lineage kin are intimate yet cast outside feudatory attachment, and the royal clan's nearness becomes more distant than the host of ministers.

sentences.zh: 先朝舊儀，草創未定，刊制律憲，垂之不朽。

translations.literal: Former court old ceremony, founded but not fixed—engrave regulations and statutes to hand down imperishably.
translations.idiomatic: The former court's old ceremony was founded but not fixed—it is time to engrave regulations and statutes to hand down imperishably.

sentences.zh: 琰之援據，甚允情理。

translations.literal: Yan Zhi's citations accord very well with sentiment and principle.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhi's citations accord very well with sentiment and principle.

sentences.zh: 可依所執。」

translations.literal: Accept what is held."
translations.idiomatic: Accept what he holds."

sentences.zh: 十二月丁未，侍中、司空公、領尚書令、任城王澄，度支尚書崔亮奏：「謹案禮記：曾子問曰：諸侯旅見天子，不得成禮者幾？

translations.literal: On the dingwei day of the twelfth month, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Minister of Works, Concurrent Master of Writing Prince Cheng of Rencheng, and Minister of Revenue Cui Liang submitted: "Respectfully examining the Record of Rites: Zengzi asked: When feudal lords travel to see the Son of Heaven but cannot complete the rite, how many cases?
translations.idiomatic: On the dingwei day of the twelfth month, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Minister of Works, Concurrent Master of Writing Prince Cheng of Rencheng, and Minister of Revenue Cui Liang submitted: "Respectfully examining the Record of Rites: Zengzi asked, When feudal lords travel to audience with the Son of Heaven but cannot complete the rite, how many cases are there?

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：四，太廟火、日蝕、后之喪、雨沾服失容則廢。

translations.literal: Confucius said: Four—the Grand Temple burns, eclipse of the sun, the empress's mourning, rain soaking robes so deportment is lost—then it is suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said: Four—the Grand Temple burns, there is an eclipse of the sun, the empress is in mourning, or rain soaks the robes so deportment is lost—then the rite is suspended.

sentences.zh: 臣等謂元日萬國賀，應是諸侯旅見之義。

translations.literal: We consider the New Year's Day when ten thousand states congratulate should be the meaning of feudal lords' travel to audience.
translations.idiomatic: We consider that the New Year's Day when the myriad states offer congratulations should be the meaning of feudal lords' travel to audience.

sentences.zh: 若禘廢朝會，孔子應云五而獨言四，明不廢朝賀也。

translations.literal: If the di were suspended and court assembly abolished, Confucius should have said five but spoke only of four—clearly court congratulations are not suspended.
translations.idiomatic: If the di were suspended and court assembly abolished, Confucius should have said five but spoke only of four—clearly court congratulations are not suspended.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄禮注云：『魯禮，三年喪畢，祫於太祖，明年春，禘羣廟。』

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan's ritual commentary says: "Lu ritual—when three-year mourning ends, he conjoins at the Grand Ancestor; next spring, di to all temples."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan's ritual commentary says: "In Lu ritual, when three-year mourning ends, one conjoins at the Grand Ancestor; the next spring, di is offered at all temples."

sentences.zh: 又鄭志：檢魯禮，春秋昭公十一年夏五月，夫人歸氏薨。

translations.literal: Also Zheng's Records: examining Lu ritual, in the eleventh year of Duke Zhao of Spring and Autumn, fifth month summer, the Lady Gui clan, the duchess, died.
translations.idiomatic: Also in Zheng's Records: examining Lu ritual, in the eleventh year of Duke Zhao in the Spring and Autumn Annals, in the fifth month of summer, the Lady of the Gui clan, the duchess, died.

sentences.zh: 十三年五月大祥，七月釋禫，公會劉子及諸侯于平丘，八月歸，不及於祫；

translations.literal: Thirteenth year, fifth month great culmination; seventh month release of provisional mourning; the duke met the Viscount Liu and feudal lords at Pingqiu; eighth month return—did not reach the conjoining;
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, the fifth month was the great culmination; in the seventh month provisional mourning was released; the duke met the Viscount Liu and the feudal lords at Pingqiu; in the eighth month he returned—too late for the conjoining;

sentences.zh: 冬，公如晉，明十四年春，歸祫，明十五年春乃禘。

translations.literal: Winter, the duke went to Jin—making clear that spring of the fourteenth year he returned for conjoining, making clear that only spring of the fifteenth year was di.
translations.idiomatic: in winter the duke went to Jin—making clear that in spring of the fourteenth year he returned for the conjoining, and that only in spring of the fifteenth year was the di performed.

sentences.zh: 經曰：『二月癸酉，有事於武宮。』

translations.literal: The classic says: "Second month guiyou, business at the Martial Shrine."
translations.idiomatic: The classic says: "In the second month, on the day guiyou, there was business at the Martial Shrine."

sentences.zh: 傳曰：『禘於武公。』

translations.literal: The commentary says: "Di to Duke Wu."
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: "Di was offered to Duke Wu."

sentences.zh: 謹案明堂位曰：『魯，王禮也。』

translations.literal: Respectfully examining Bright Hall Positions: "Lu had king ritual."
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully examining Bright Hall Positions: "Lu practiced king ritual."

sentences.zh: 喪畢祫禘，似有退理。

translations.literal: Conjoining and di after mourning ends seems to have reasoning for deferral.
translations.idiomatic: Conjoining and di after mourning ends seems to allow reasoning for deferral.

sentences.zh: 詳考古禮，未有以祭事廢元會者。

translations.literal: Examining ancient ritual in detail, never has sacrificial business suspended the New Year assembly.
translations.idiomatic: Examining ancient ritual in detail, there is no precedent for suspending the New Year assembly because of sacrificial business.

sentences.zh: 禮云『吉事先近日』，脫不吉，容改筮三旬。

translations.literal: The Rites say "auspicious affairs should be moved to a nearer day"—if not auspicious, one may change the divination within thirty days.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites say "auspicious affairs should be moved to a nearer day"—if the day is inauspicious, the divination may be changed within thirty days.

sentences.zh: 尋攝太史令趙翼等列稱，正月二十六日祭亦吉。

translations.literal: Pursuing Acting Grand Astrologer Zhao Yi and others who listed and stated the twenty-sixth day of the first month is also auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing the report of Acting Grand Astrologer Zhao Yi and others, who listed and stated that the twenty-sixth day of the first month is also auspicious.

sentences.zh: 請移禘祀在中旬十四日，時祭移二十六日，猶曰春禘，又非退義。

translations.literal: We request moving the di sacrifice to the fourteenth day of the month's middle ten days, moving the seasonal sacrifice to the twenty-sixth—it is still called spring di, and not deferral in meaning.
translations.idiomatic: We request moving the di sacrifice to the fourteenth day of the month's middle ten days and moving the seasonal sacrifice to the twenty-sixth—it would still be called spring di, and would not constitute deferral in meaning.

sentences.zh: 祭則無疏怠之譏，三元有順軌之美。

translations.literal: For sacrifice there would be no censure of neglect; for the Three Origins there would be the beauty of orderly track.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice would incur no censure of neglect, and the Three Origins would retain the beauty of an orderly course.

sentences.zh: 既被成旨，宜即宣行。

translations.literal: Having received approved intent, it should at once be announced and carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Having received approved intent, this should at once be announced and carried out.

sentences.zh: 臣等伏度國之大事，在祀與戎。

translations.literal: We bow and estimate: the great affairs of the state lie in sacrifice and war.
translations.idiomatic: We bow and consider that the great affairs of the state lie in sacrifice and war.

sentences.zh: 君舉必書，恐貽後誚。

translations.literal: The ruler's every act must be recorded, lest later blame be incurred.
translations.idiomatic: Every act of the ruler must be recorded, lest blame fall on us from posterity.

sentences.zh: 輒訪引古籍，竊有未安。

translations.literal: Repeatedly consulting and citing ancient texts, I privately am not at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Having repeatedly consulted and cited ancient texts, I am privately not at ease with this.

sentences.zh: 臣等學缺通經，識不稽古，備位樞納，可否必陳。

translations.literal: We, your subjects, are deficient in learning and do not penetrate the classics; our knowledge does not examine antiquity; we fill posts at the pivot gate; approval or rejection must be stated.
translations.idiomatic: We are deficient in learning and do not master the classics; our knowledge does not rest on antiquity; we merely fill posts at the pivot gate, yet we must state our approval or rejection.

sentences.zh: 冒陳所見，伏聽裁衷。」

translations.literal: We presumptuously present what we have seen and bow to hear the balanced decision."
translations.idiomatic: We presumptuously present our views and bow to await Your Majesty's balanced decision."

sentences.zh: 靈太后令曰：「可如所執。」

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling ordered: "It may follow what was held."
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling ordered: "Let it be as you have argued."

sentences.zh: 初，世宗永平、延昌中，欲建明堂。

translations.literal: At the beginning, in the Yongping and Yanzhang periods of Emperor Shizong, they wished to build the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Yongping and Yanzhang periods under Emperor Xuanwu, there was a plan to build the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 而議者或云五室，或云九室，頻屬年饑，遂寢。

translations.literal: But debaters said either five chambers or nine chambers; repeatedly it fell in years of famine, and the matter was laid to rest.
translations.idiomatic: Debaters argued either for five chambers or for nine chambers, but repeated years of famine caused the project to be laid aside.

sentences.zh: 至是復議之，詔從五室。

translations.literal: At this time it was debated again, and an edict followed the five chambers.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the matter was debated again, and an edict adopted the five-chamber plan.

sentences.zh: 及元叉執政，遂改營九室。

translations.literal: When Yuan Cha held power, they then changed to construct nine chambers.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Cha came to power, the construction was changed to nine chambers.

sentences.zh: 值世亂不成，宗配之禮，迄無所設。

translations.literal: Meeting with worldly disorder it was not completed; the rites of ancestral matching, to the end were nowhere established.
translations.idiomatic: Worldly disorder prevented completion, and the rites of ancestral matching were never established.

sentences.zh: 神龜初，靈太后父司徒胡國珍薨，贈太上秦公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shengui era, the Empress Dowager Ling's father, Minister of Education Hu Guozhen, died, and was posthumously enfeoffed as the Supreme Duke of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shengui era, Hu Guozhen, the Empress Dowager Ling's father and Minister of Education, died and was posthumously enfeoffed as the Supreme Duke of Qin.

sentences.zh: 時疑其廟制。

translations.literal: At the time there was doubt about the regulations for his ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there was uncertainty about the regulations for his ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 太學博士王延業議曰：案王制云：諸侯祭二昭二穆，與太祖之廟而五。

translations.literal: Erudite of the Imperial Academy Wang Yanye proposed: Investigating the Royal Regulations, it says: feudal lords sacrifice to two zhao and two mu, together with the Grand Ancestor's temple making five.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite of the Imperial Academy Wang Yanye proposed: According to the Royal Regulations, feudal lords sacrifice to two zhao and two mu, together with the Grand Ancestor's temple, making five in all.

sentences.zh: 又小記云：王者立四廟。

translations.literal: Also the Lesser Record says: the king establishes four temples.
translations.idiomatic: The Lesser Record also says: the king establishes four temples.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄云：「高祖已下，與始祖而五。」

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan said: "From the High Ancestor down, together with the founding ancestor making five."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan said: "From the High Ancestor down, together with the founding ancestor, making five."

sentences.zh: 明立廟之正，以親為限，不過於四。

translations.literal: This clarifies the standard for establishing temples: taking kinship as the limit, not exceeding four.
translations.idiomatic: This clarifies the standard for establishing temples: kinship sets the limit, and the number does not exceed four.

sentences.zh: 其外有大功者，然後為祖宗。

translations.literal: Beyond these, those with great merit, only then become zong and miao.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond these, only those with great merit become zong and miao.

sentences.zh: 然則無太祖者，止於四世，有太祖乃得為五，禮之正文也。

translations.literal: Thus without a Grand Ancestor, one stops at four generations; with a Grand Ancestor one may have five—the main text of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Thus without a Grand Ancestor one stops at four generations; with a Grand Ancestor one may have five—this is the main text of ritual.

sentences.zh: 文王世子云：「五廟之孫，祖廟未毀，雖為庶人，冠、娶妻必告。」

translations.literal: Heir of King Wen says: "A descendant of five temples, while the zu temple is not destroyed, though a commoner, capping and taking a wife must be reported."
translations.idiomatic: Heir of King Wen says: "A descendant of five temples, while the zu temple is not retired, though reduced to commoner status, capping and taking a wife must be reported."

sentences.zh: 鄭玄云：「實四廟而言五廟者，容高祖為始封君之子。」

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan said: "Actually four temples but saying five temples—allowing the High Ancestor as son of the first enfeoffed lord."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan said: "There are actually four temples but one speaks of five—this allows the High Ancestor to be the son of the first enfeoffed lord."

sentences.zh: [8]明始封之君，在四世之外，正位太祖，乃得稱五廟之孫。

translations.literal: [8] This clarifies that the first enfeoffed lord, outside the four generations, occupying the correct position of Grand Ancestor, only then may be called a descendant of five temples.
translations.idiomatic: [8] This clarifies that the first enfeoffed lord, standing outside the four generations and occupying the correct position as Grand Ancestor, only then may be called a descendant of five temples.

sentences.zh: 若未有太祖，已祀五世，則鄭無為釋高祖為始封君之子也。
