translations.literal: If there is not yet a Grand Ancestor but five generations are already sacrificed to, then Zheng would have no reason to explain the High Ancestor as son of the first enfeoffed lord.
translations.idiomatic: If there is not yet a Grand Ancestor but five generations are already being sacrificed to, then Zheng would have no reason to explain the High Ancestor as the son of the first enfeoffed lord.

sentences.zh: 此先儒精義，當今顯證也。

translations.literal: This is the refined meaning of former Confucians and a clear proof for the present age.
translations.idiomatic: This is the refined meaning of the former Confucians and clear proof for our own case.

sentences.zh: 又喪服傳曰：「若公子之子孫，有封為國君者，則世世祖是人也，不祖公子。」

translations.literal: Also the Mourning Garment Tradition says: "If a grandson of a lord's son is enfeoffed as state ruler, then generation after generation they take this man as ancestor and do not take the lord's son as ancestor."
translations.idiomatic: The Mourning Garment Tradition also says: "If a grandson of a lord's son is enfeoffed as state ruler, then generation after generation they take this man as ancestor and do not take the lord's son as ancestor."

sentences.zh: 鄭玄云：「謂後世為君者，祖此受封之君，不得祀別子也。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan said: "This means that later generations who become rulers take this enfeoffed lord as ancestor and may not sacrifice to the separate son.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan said: "This means that later generations who become rulers take this enfeoffed lord as ancestor and may not sacrifice to the separate son.

sentences.zh: 公子若在高祖已下，則如其親服，後世遷之，乃毀其廟爾。」

translations.literal: If the lord's son is below the High Ancestor, then according to his degree of kinship; in later generations he is moved, and only then is his temple destroyed."
translations.idiomatic: If the lord's son ranks below the High Ancestor, mourning follows the degree of kinship; in later generations he is moved, and only then is his temple destroyed."

sentences.zh: 明始封猶在親限，故祀止高祖。

translations.literal: This clarifies that the first enfeoffment is still within the kin limit, so sacrifice stops at the High Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: This clarifies that the first enfeoffment is still within the kin limit, so sacrifice stops at the High Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 又云如親而遷，尤知高祖之父，不立廟矣。

translations.literal: It also says that when moved according to kinship, one especially knows that the High Ancestor's father does not receive a temple.
translations.idiomatic: It also says that when tablets are moved according to kinship, one especially knows that the High Ancestor's father does not receive a temple.

sentences.zh: 此又立廟明法，與今事相當者也。

translations.literal: This is again the clear law for establishing temples and corresponds to the present matter.
translations.idiomatic: This is again the clear law for establishing temples and corresponds to the present case.

sentences.zh: 又禮緯云：「夏四廟，至子孫五。

translations.literal: Also the Ritual Apocrypha says: "Xia had four temples; by descendants, five.
translations.idiomatic: The Ritual Apocrypha also says: "Xia had four temples; by descendants, five.

sentences.zh: 殷五廟，至子孫六。」

translations.literal: Yin had five temples; by descendants, six."
translations.idiomatic: Yin had five temples; by descendants, six."

sentences.zh: 注云：「言至子孫，則初時未備也。」

translations.literal: The commentary says: "Speaking of descendants means that at first it was not yet complete."
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: "Speaking of descendants means that at first the arrangement was not yet complete."

sentences.zh: 此又顯在緯籍，區別若斯者也。

translations.literal: This is again clearly in the apocryphal texts, with distinctions as precise as this.
translations.idiomatic: This distinction is again clearly recorded in the apocryphal texts.

sentences.zh: 又晉初，以宣帝是始封之君，應為太祖，而以猶在祖位，故唯祀征西已下六世。

translations.literal: Also at the beginning of Jin, because Emperor Xuan was the first enfeoffed lord and should be Grand Ancestor, yet because he still occupied the zu position, they only sacrificed from Lord of the Campaign West down through six generations.
translations.idiomatic: Also at the beginning of Jin, because Emperor Xuan was the first enfeoffed lord and should have been Grand Ancestor, yet because he still occupied the zu position, they sacrificed only from the Lord of the Campaign West down through six generations.

sentences.zh: 待世世相推，宣帝出居太祖之位，然後七廟乃備。

translations.literal: Awaiting generation after generation of promotion, when Emperor Xuan moved out to occupy the Grand Ancestor's position, only then were the seven temples complete.
translations.idiomatic: Only after generation upon generation of promotion, when Emperor Xuan moved out to occupy the Grand Ancestor's position, were the seven temples complete.

sentences.zh: 此又依準前軌，若重規襲矩者也。

translations.literal: This again follows the former track, like overlapping compasses and repeated squares.
translations.idiomatic: This again follows the former precedent, like overlapping compasses and repeated squares.

sentences.zh: 竊謂太祖者，功高業大，百世不遷，故親廟之外，特更崇立。

translations.literal: I venture to say that the Grand Ancestor has lofty merit and great achievement, not moved for a hundred generations; therefore beyond the kin temples he is specially exalted and established.
translations.idiomatic: I venture to say that the Grand Ancestor has lofty merit and great achievement and is not moved for a hundred generations; therefore beyond the kin temples he is specially exalted and established.

sentences.zh: 苟無其功，不可獨居正位，而遽見遷毀。

translations.literal: If without such merit, one may not alone occupy the correct position, yet suddenly see moving and destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Without such merit one may not alone occupy the correct position, yet would suddenly be subject to moving and destruction.

sentences.zh: 且三世已前，廟及於五；

translations.literal: Moreover, before the third generation, temples reach five;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, before the third generation, temples may reach five;

sentences.zh: 玄孫已後，祀止於四。

translations.literal: after the great-great-grandson, sacrifice stops at four.
translations.idiomatic: after the great-great-grandson, sacrifice stops at four.

sentences.zh: 一與一奪，名位莫定，求之典禮，所未前聞。

translations.literal: One given and one taken away, name and position not fixed—seeking this in canonical ritual, never heard before.
translations.idiomatic: One generation granted a temple and the next denied one—name and position unsettled; seeking this in canonical ritual, it has never been heard of before.

sentences.zh: 今太上秦公，疏爵列土，大啟河山，傳祚無窮，永同帶礪，實有始封之功，方成不遷之廟。

translations.literal: Now the Supreme Lord Duke of Qin, enfeoffed with noble rank and granted territory, greatly opened rivers and mountains, transmitted the throne without end, forever like girdle and whetstone, truly had the merit of first enfeoffment and is just forming an unmoved temple.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Supreme Lord Duke of Qin, enfeoffed with noble rank and granted territory, greatly opened rivers and mountains, transmitted the throne without end, secure as girdle and whetstone, truly had the merit of first enfeoffment and is just forming an unmoved temple.

sentences.zh: 但親在四世之內，名班昭穆之序，雖應為太祖，而尚在禰位，不可遠探高祖之父，以合五者之數。

translations.literal: But kin is within four generations, name ranked in the zhao-mu sequence; though he should be Grand Ancestor, he is still in the mi position; one may not far seek the High Ancestor's father to match the number five.
translations.idiomatic: But his kinship falls within four generations and his name ranks in the zhao-mu sequence; though he should be Grand Ancestor, he is still in the mi position, and one may not reach back to the High Ancestor's father to make up the number five.

sentences.zh: 太祖之室，當須世世相推，親盡之後，乃出居正位，以備五廟之典。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor's chamber must await generation after generation of promotion; after kin is exhausted, only then does he move out to the correct position to complete the canon of five temples.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor's chamber must await generation after generation of promotion; only after kin is exhausted does he move out to the correct position to complete the canon of five temples.

sentences.zh: 夫循文責實，理貴允當，考創宗祊，得禮為美。

translations.literal: Now, following the text and seeking the fact, principle values what is fitting; examining the founding of the ancestral shrine, obtaining ritual is beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: Following the text and seeking the fact, principle values what is fitting; in examining the founding of the ancestral shrine, conforming to ritual is what is beautiful.

sentences.zh: 不可苟薦虛名，取榮多數，求之經記，竊謂為允。

translations.literal: One may not hastily recommend empty names and take glory in a greater number; seeking this in the classics, I venture to say it is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: One may not hastily recommend empty names and take glory in a greater number; seeking this in the classics, I venture to say this is fitting.

sentences.zh: 又武始侯本無采地，於皇朝制令，名準大夫。

translations.literal: Also the Marquis of Wushi originally had no fief; under the imperial court's regulations his title matches a grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Also the Marquis of Wushi originally had no fief; under the imperial court's regulations his title matches that of a grandee.

sentences.zh: 案如禮意，諸侯奪宗，武始四時蒸嘗，宜於秦公之廟。

translations.literal: Investigating according to ritual meaning, when feudal lords seize the lineage, Wushi's four-season offerings should be at the Duke of Qin's temple.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating according to ritual meaning, when feudal lords seize the lineage, Wushi's four-season offerings should be performed at the Duke of Qin's temple.

sentences.zh: 博士盧觀議：

translations.literal: Erudite Lu Guan argued:
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Lu Guan argued:

sentences.zh: 案王制：天子七廟，三昭三穆，與太祖之廟而七；

translations.literal: Investigating the Royal Regulations: the Son of Heaven has seven temples—three zhao and three mu, together with the Grand Ancestor's temple making seven;
translations.idiomatic: Investigating the Royal Regulations: the Son of Heaven has seven temples—three zhao and three mu, together with the Grand Ancestor's temple, making seven;

sentences.zh: 諸侯五廟，二昭二穆，與太祖之廟而五；

translations.literal: feudal lords have five temples—two zhao and two mu, together with the Grand Ancestor's temple making five;
translations.idiomatic: feudal lords have five temples—two zhao and two mu, together with the Grand Ancestor's temple, making five;

sentences.zh: 大夫三；

translations.literal: grandees, three;
translations.idiomatic: grandees, three;

sentences.zh: 士一。

translations.literal: knights, one.
translations.idiomatic: knights, one.

sentences.zh: 自上已下，降殺以兩，庶人無廟，死為鬼焉。

translations.literal: From the superior down, reduction proceeds by twos; commoners have no temple—when dead they become ghosts.
translations.idiomatic: From the superior down, reduction proceeds by twos; commoners have no temple—when dead they become ghosts.

sentences.zh: 故曰，尊者統遠，卑者統近。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: the honored unite the distant, the lowly unite the near.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore it is said: the honored unite the distant, the lowly unite the near.

sentences.zh: 是以諸侯及太祖，天子及其祖之所自出。

translations.literal: Thus for feudal lords it reaches to the Grand Ancestor; for the Son of Heaven it reaches to the ancestor from whom his ancestor sprang.
translations.idiomatic: Thus for feudal lords sacrifice reaches to the Grand Ancestor; for the Son of Heaven it reaches to the ancestor from whom his ancestor sprang.

sentences.zh: 祭法曰：「諸侯立五廟，一壇一墠，曰考廟，曰王考廟，曰皇考廟，皆月祭之。

translations.literal: The Law of Sacrifice says: "Feudal lords establish five temples, one altar and one mound: the temple of the father, the temple of the grandfather, the temple of the great-grandfather—all receive monthly sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The Law of Sacrifice says: "Feudal lords establish five temples, one altar and one mound: the temple of the father, the temple of the grandfather, the temple of the great-grandfather—all receive monthly sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 顯考廟，祖考廟，享嘗乃止。

translations.literal: The temple of the distinguished father and the temple of the ancestral father—offerings stop at the seasonal feasts.
translations.idiomatic: The temple of the distinguished father and the temple of the ancestral father receive offerings only at the seasonal feasts.

sentences.zh: 去祖為壇，去壇為墠，去墠為鬼。」

translations.literal: When the ancestor departs, there is an altar; when the altar departs, there is a mound; when the mound departs, there is a ghost."
translations.idiomatic: When the ancestor departs, there is an altar; when the altar departs, there is a mound; when the mound departs, there is a ghost."

sentences.zh: 至於禘祫，方合食太祖之宮。

translations.literal: As for di and conjoining, only then is there shared feasting at the Grand Ancestor's palace.
translations.idiomatic: As for di and conjoining, only then is there shared feasting at the Grand Ancestor's palace.

sentences.zh: 大傳曰：「別子為祖。」

translations.literal: The Great Tradition says: "The separate son becomes ancestor."
translations.idiomatic: The Great Tradition says: "The separate son becomes ancestor."

sentences.zh: 喪服傳曰：「公子不得禰先君，公孫不得祖諸侯。」

translations.literal: The Mourning Garment Tradition says: "The lord's son may not take the former ruler as mi; the lord's grandson may not take the feudal lord as zu."
translations.idiomatic: The Mourning Garment Tradition says: "The lord's son may not take the former ruler as mi; the lord's grandson may not take the feudal lord as zu."

sentences.zh: 鄭說不得祖禰者，不得立其廟而祭之也；

translations.literal: Zheng's explanation of "may not take as zu or mi" means one may not establish their temples and sacrifice to them;
translations.idiomatic: Zheng's explanation of "may not take as zu or mi" means one may not establish their temples and sacrifice to them;

sentences.zh: 世世祖是人者，謂世世祖受封之君；

translations.literal: "generation after generation they take this man as ancestor" means generation after generation they take the enfeoffed lord as ancestor;
translations.idiomatic: "generation after generation they take this man as ancestor" means generation after generation they take the enfeoffed lord as ancestor;

sentences.zh: 不得祖公子者，後世為君者，祖此受封之君，不得祀別子也；

translations.literal: "may not take the lord's son as ancestor" means that later generations who become rulers take this enfeoffed lord as ancestor and may not sacrifice to the separate son;
translations.idiomatic: "may not take the lord's son as ancestor" means that later generations who become rulers take this enfeoffed lord as ancestor and may not sacrifice to the separate son;

sentences.zh: 公子若在高祖以下，則如其親服，後世遷之，乃毀其廟耳。

translations.literal: if the lord's son is below the High Ancestor, then according to his degree of kinship; in later generations he is moved, and only then is his temple destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: if the lord's son ranks below the High Ancestor, mourning follows the degree of kinship; in later generations he is moved, and only then is his temple destroyed.

sentences.zh: 愚以為遷者，遷於太祖廟，毀者從太祖而毀之。

translations.literal: I deem that "moved" means moved to the Grand Ancestor's temple; "destroyed" means destroyed following the Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: I deem that "moved" means moved to the Grand Ancestor's temple, and "destroyed" means destroyed following the Grand Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 若不遷太祖，不須發祖是人之文；

translations.literal: If the Grand Ancestor is not moved, there is no need to set forth the text about taking this man as ancestor;
translations.idiomatic: If the Grand Ancestor is not moved, there is no need to set forth the text about taking this man as ancestor;

sentences.zh: [9]明非始封，故復見乃毀之節。

translations.literal: [9] this clarifies that it is not first enfeoffment, so one again sees the section on destruction.
translations.idiomatic: [9] this clarifies that it is not first enfeoffment, so one again sees the section on destruction.

sentences.zh: 何以知之？

translations.literal: How does one know this?
translations.idiomatic: How does one know this?

sentences.zh: 案諸侯有祖考之廟，祭五世之禮。

translations.literal: Investigating: feudal lords have the temple of the ancestral father—the rite of sacrificing to five generations.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating the texts: feudal lords have the temple of the ancestral father—the rite of sacrificing to five generations.

sentences.zh: 五禮正祖為輕，一朝頓立。

translations.literal: Among the five ritual ranks the correct ancestor is light; in one morning it is suddenly established.
translations.idiomatic: Among the five ritual ranks the correct ancestor is the lesser case; in one morning it is suddenly established.

sentences.zh: 而祖考之廟，要待六世之君，六世已前，虛而蔑主。

translations.literal: But the temple of the ancestral father must await the ruler of the sixth generation; before the sixth generation, it is empty and the spirit lord is slighted.
translations.idiomatic: But the temple of the ancestral father must await the ruler of the sixth generation; before the sixth generation it stands empty and the spirit lord is slighted.

sentences.zh: 求之聖旨，未為通論。

translations.literal: Seeking this in the sage's intent, it is not a penetrating discourse.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking this in the sage's intent, it is not a penetrating argument.

sentences.zh: 曾子問曰：「廟無虛主。」

translations.literal: Zengzi asked: "A temple has no empty spirit lord."
translations.idiomatic: Zengzi asked: "A temple has no empty spirit lord."

sentences.zh: 虛主唯四，祖考不與焉。

translations.literal: Empty spirit lords are only four; the ancestral father is not among them.
translations.idiomatic: Empty spirit lords number only four; the ancestral father is not among them.

sentences.zh: 明太祖之廟，必不空置。

translations.literal: This clarifies that the Grand Ancestor's temple must not be left empty.
translations.idiomatic: This clarifies that the Grand Ancestor's temple must not be left empty.

sentences.zh: 禮緯曰：「夏四廟，至子孫五；

translations.literal: The Ritual Apocrypha says: "Xia had four temples; by descendants, five;
translations.idiomatic: The Ritual Apocrypha says: "Xia had four temples; by descendants, five;

sentences.zh: 殷五廟，至子孫六；

translations.literal: Yin had five temples; by descendants, six;
translations.idiomatic: Yin had five temples; by descendants, six;

sentences.zh: 周六廟，至子孫七。」

translations.literal: Zhou had six temples; by descendants, seven."
translations.idiomatic: Zhou had six temples; by descendants, seven."

sentences.zh: 見夏無始祖，待禹而五；

translations.literal: This shows Xia had no founding ancestor; awaiting Yu, there were five;
translations.idiomatic: This shows Xia had no founding ancestor; awaiting Yu, there were five;

sentences.zh: 殷人郊契，得湯而六；

translations.literal: the Yin people sacrificed to Qi at the border; obtaining Tang, there were six;
translations.idiomatic: the Yin people sacrificed to Qi at the border; obtaining Tang, there were six;

sentences.zh: 周有后稷，及文王至武王而七。

translations.literal: Zhou had Hou Ji, and from King Wen to King Wu there were seven.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou had Hou Ji, and from King Wen to King Wu there were seven.

sentences.zh: 言夏即大禹之身，言子謂啟、誦之世，言孫是迭遷之時。

translations.literal: Speaking of Xia means the body of Great Yu; speaking of son means the age of Qi and Zhong Kang; speaking of grandson is the time of successive transfer.
translations.idiomatic: Speaking of Xia means the lifetime of Great Yu; speaking of son means the age of Qi and Zhong Kang; speaking of grandson means the time of successive transfer.

sentences.zh: 禹為受命，不毀親；

translations.literal: Yu received the mandate and did not destroy kin;
translations.idiomatic: Yu received the mandate and did not destroy kin;

sentences.zh: 湯為始君，不遷五主；

translations.literal: Tang was the founding ruler and did not move the five lords;
translations.idiomatic: Tang was the founding ruler and did not move the five lords;

sentences.zh: 文武為二祧，亦不去三昭三穆。

translations.literal: Wen and Wu were the two tiao, yet they did not remove the three zhao and three mu.
translations.idiomatic: Wen and Wu were the two tiao, yet they did not remove the three zhao and three mu.

sentences.zh: 三昭三穆謂通文武，若無文武，親不過四。

translations.literal: The three zhao and three mu mean extending through Wen and Wu; without Wen and Wu, kin does not exceed four.
translations.idiomatic: The three zhao and three mu mean extending through Wen and Wu; without Wen and Wu, kin does not exceed four.

sentences.zh: 觀遠祖漢侍中植所說云然，鄭玄、馬昭亦皆同爾。

translations.literal: Examining what the distant ancestor Han Palace Attendant Zhi said, it is so; Zheng Xuan and Ma Zhao also all agree.
translations.idiomatic: Examining what the distant ancestor Han Palace Attendant Zhi said, it is so; Zheng Xuan and Ma Zhao also all agree.

sentences.zh: 且天子逆加二祧，得并為七。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Son of Heaven inversely adds two tiao and thereby obtains seven together.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Son of Heaven retroactively adds two tiao and thereby obtains seven together.

sentences.zh: 諸侯預立太祖，何為不得為五乎？

translations.literal: If feudal lords pre-establish the Grand Ancestor, why may they not have five?
translations.idiomatic: If feudal lords pre-establish the Grand Ancestor, why may they not have five?

sentences.zh: 今始封君子之立禰廟，頗似成王之於二祧。

translations.literal: Now the first enfeoffed lord's establishing the mi temple greatly resembles King Cheng's relation to the two tiao.
translations.idiomatic: Now the first enfeoffed lord's establishing the mi temple greatly resembles King Cheng's relation to the two tiao.

sentences.zh: 孫卿曰：「有天下者事七世，有一國者事五世。」

translations.literal: Xunzi said: "One who possesses All-under-Heaven serves seven generations; one who possesses a single state serves five generations."
translations.idiomatic: Xunzi said: "One who possesses All-under-Heaven serves seven generations; one who possesses a single state serves five generations."

sentences.zh: 假使八世，天子乃得事七；

translations.literal: Supposing eight generations, only then may the Son of Heaven serve seven;
translations.idiomatic: Supposing eight generations, only then may the Son of Heaven serve seven;

sentences.zh: 六世，諸侯方通祭五；

translations.literal: six generations, and feudal lords only then fully sacrifice to five;
translations.idiomatic: six generations, and feudal lords only then fully sacrifice to five;

sentences.zh: 推情準理，不其謬乎！

translations.literal: weighing sentiment against principle—is it not absurd!
translations.idiomatic: weighing sentiment against principle—is it not absurd!

sentences.zh: 雖王侯用禮，文節不同，三隅反之，自然昭灼。

translations.literal: Although kings and marquises use ritual and literary forms differ, from three corners one turns back and it is naturally luminous.
translations.idiomatic: Although kings and marquises use ritual and the literary forms differ, inferring from one corner to three, the principle is naturally luminous.

sentences.zh: 且文宣公方為太祖，世居子孫，今立五廟，竊謂為是。

translations.literal: Moreover, Duke Wenxuan is just becoming Grand Ancestor, dwelling in descendants for generations; now to establish five temples, I venture to say it is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Duke Wenxuan is just becoming Grand Ancestor, dwelling among descendants for generations; to establish five temples now, I venture to say it is correct.

sentences.zh: 禮緯又云：「諸侯五廟，親四，始祖一。」

translations.literal: The Ritual Apocrypha also says: "Feudal lords have five temples—four for kin, one for the founding ancestor."
translations.idiomatic: The Ritual Apocrypha also says: "Feudal lords have five temples—four for kin, one for the founding ancestor."

sentences.zh: 明始封之君或上或下，[10]雖未居正室，無廢四祀之親。

translations.literal: This clarifies that the first enfeoffed lord may be above or below, [10] and though not yet occupying the main chamber, the four sacrifices to kin are not abolished.
translations.idiomatic: This clarifies that the first enfeoffed lord may rank above or below, [10] and though not yet occupying the main chamber, the four sacrifices to kin are not abolished.

sentences.zh: 小記曰：「王者禘其祖之所自出，以其祖配之，而立四廟。」

translations.literal: The Lesser Record says: "The king performs di to the ancestor from whom his ancestor sprang, matching him with his ancestor, and establishes four temples."
translations.idiomatic: The Lesser Record says: "The king performs di to the ancestor from whom his ancestor sprang, matching him with his ancestor, and establishes four temples."

sentences.zh: 此實殷湯時制，不為難也。

translations.literal: This was truly the system of the Yin at Tang's time and is not difficult.
translations.idiomatic: This was truly the system of the Yin at Tang's time and is not difficult to apply.

sentences.zh: 聊復摽牓，略引章條。

translations.literal: For the moment I again post notices, briefly citing the articles and clauses.
translations.idiomatic: I shall post this summary once more and briefly cite the relevant articles.

sentences.zh: 愚戇不足以待大問。

translations.literal: My foolish bluntness is insufficient to await great questioning.
translations.idiomatic: My dull wits are hardly fit to bear scrutiny on so weighty a matter.

sentences.zh: 侍中、太傅、清河王懌議：

translations.literal: Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand Tutor, Prince of Qinghe Yi argued:
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand Tutor, and Prince of Qinghe Yi argued:

sentences.zh: 太學博士王延業及盧觀等，各率異見。

translations.literal: Erudite of the Imperial Academy Wang Yanye and Lu Guan and others each led differing views.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite of the Imperial Academy Wang Yanye and Lu Guan and others each offered differing views.

sentences.zh: 案禮記王制：「天子七廟，三昭三穆，與太祖之廟而七；

translations.literal: Investigating the "Royal Regulations" in the Book of Rites: "The Son of Heaven has seven temples—three zhao and three mu, with the Grand Ancestor's temple making seven;
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Rites, "Royal Regulations," states: "The Son of Heaven has seven temples—three zhao and three mu, which with the Grand Ancestor's temple make seven;

sentences.zh: 諸侯五廟，二昭二穆，與太祖之廟而五。」

translations.literal: feudal lords have five temples—two zhao and two mu, with the Grand Ancestor's temple making five."
translations.idiomatic: feudal lords have five temples—two zhao and two mu, which with the Grand Ancestor's temple make five."

sentences.zh: 並是後世追論備廟之文，皆非當時據立神位之事也。

translations.literal: These are all texts of later ages retrospectively discussing complete temples; none are matters of actually establishing spirit seats at the time.
translations.idiomatic: These are all texts of later ages retrospectively discussing complete temples; none describe actually establishing spirit seats at the time.

sentences.zh: 良由去聖久遠，經禮殘缺，諸儒注記，典制無因。

translations.literal: Truly because one has been far from the sages for so long, the classic rites are fragmented and defective, and the various Ruists' commentaries and records have no basis for institutional norms.
translations.idiomatic: Truly because the age has long been far from the sages, the canonical rites are broken and incomplete, and the Ruists' commentaries and records offer no firm basis for institutional norms.

sentences.zh: 雖稽考異聞，引證古誼，然用捨從世，通塞有時，折衷取正，固難詳矣。

translations.literal: Although one examines divergent accounts and cites ancient meaning, yet adoption and rejection follow the age, penetration and blockage have their seasons—to strike the mean and take what is correct is inherently hard to exhaust.
translations.idiomatic: One may sift divergent accounts and invoke ancient principles, yet what is kept or cast aside follows the age, and what opens or closes has its season; to strike the mean and fix the right rule is, in the end, hard to settle with certainty.

sentences.zh: 今相國、秦公初搆國廟，追立神位，唯當仰祀二昭二穆，上極高曾，四世而已。

translations.literal: Now the Chancellor and Duke of Qin are first constructing the state temple and retroactively establishing spirit seats; one should only look upward and sacrifice to two zhao and two mu, reaching at most to the High Ancestor and Great-Great-Grandfather—four generations only.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the Chancellor and Duke of Qin are first building the state temple and retroactively establishing spirit seats, sacrifice should look upward only to two zhao and two mu, reaching at most to the High Ancestor and Great-Great-Grandfather—four generations in all.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: How so?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this?

sentences.zh: 秦公身是始封之君，將為不遷之祖。

translations.literal: The Duke of Qin in person is the first enfeoffed lord and will become the unmoved ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Qin himself is the first enfeoffed lord and will become the unmoved ancestor.

sentences.zh: 若以功業隆重，越居正室，恐以卑臨尊，亂昭穆也。

translations.literal: If because his achievements are weighty he oversteps into the main chamber, I fear the base will preside over the honored and disorder the zhao and mu.
translations.idiomatic: If, because his achievements are weighty, he is placed above in the main chamber, I fear the low will preside over the high and disorder the zhao and mu sequence.

sentences.zh: 如其權立始祖，以備五廟，恐數滿便毀，非禮意也。

translations.literal: If one provisionally establishes the founding ancestor to complete the five temples, I fear that when the count is full they will at once be destroyed—this is not the ritual intent.
translations.idiomatic: If one provisionally establishes the founding ancestor to complete the five temples, I fear that once the number is full they will immediately be retired—this is not the ritual intent.

sentences.zh: 昔司馬懿立功於魏，為晉太祖，及至子晉公昭，乃立五廟，亦祀四世，止於高曾。

translations.literal: In former times Sima Yi established merit in Wei and became Grand Ancestor of Jin; it was only at his son, Duke of Jin Zhao, that five temples were established, yet they also sacrificed to four generations, stopping at the High Ancestor and Great-Great-Grandfather.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Sima Yi won merit in Wei and became Grand Ancestor of Jin; only under his son, Duke of Jin Zhao, were five temples established, yet sacrifice still reached four generations, stopping at the High Ancestor and Great-Great-Grandfather.

sentences.zh: 太祖之位，虛俟宣、文，待其後裔，數滿乃止。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor's seat was left vacant awaiting Xuan and Wen; it awaited their descendants, and only when the count was full did it stop.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor's seat was left vacant awaiting Xuan and Wen; it awaited their descendants, and only when the number was full did the arrangement cease.

sentences.zh: 此亦前代之成事，方今所殷鑒也。

translations.literal: This too is a accomplished affair of a former age—the mirror for the present.
translations.idiomatic: This too is a settled precedent of former ages—the mirror the present should heed.

sentences.zh: 又禮緯云：「夏四廟，至子孫五；

translations.literal: Moreover, the Ritual Apocrypha says: "Xia had four temples; by descendants, five;
translations.idiomatic: The Ritual Apocrypha also records: "Xia had four temples; in descendant generations, five;

sentences.zh: 殷五廟，至子孫六；

translations.literal: Yin had five temples; by descendants, six;
translations.idiomatic: Yin had five temples; by descendants, six;

sentences.zh: 周六廟，至子孫七。」

translations.literal: Zhou had six temples; by descendants, seven."
translations.idiomatic: Zhou had six temples; by descendants, seven."

sentences.zh: 明知當時太祖之神，仍依昭穆之序，要待子孫，世世相推，然後太祖出居正位耳。

translations.literal: This clearly shows that at the time the spirit of the Grand Ancestor still followed the order of zhao and mu; it had to await descendants, generation after generation pushing forward, and only then did the Grand Ancestor emerge to occupy the main position.
translations.idiomatic: This clearly shows that at the time the Grand Ancestor's spirit still followed the zhao and mu order; it had to await descendants, generation after generation advancing, and only then did the Grand Ancestor emerge to occupy the main position.

sentences.zh: 遠稽禮緯諸儒所說，近循晉公之廟故事，宜依博士王延業議，定立四主，親止高曾，且虛太祖之位，以待子孫而備五廟焉。

translations.literal: Investigating afar what the Ritual Apocrypha and various Ruists say, and following near at hand the precedent of the Duke of Jin's temple, one should follow Erudite Wang Yanye's proposal: fix and establish four tablet-lords, kin stopping at the High Ancestor and Great-Great-Grandfather, and moreover leave the Grand Ancestor's seat vacant to await descendants and thereby complete the five temples.
translations.idiomatic: Looking afar to what the Ritual Apocrypha and the Ruists say, and near at hand to the precedent of the Duke of Jin's temple, one should follow Erudite Wang Yanye's proposal: establish four tablet-lords, kin stopping at the High Ancestor and Great-Great-Grandfather, and leave the Grand Ancestor's seat vacant to await descendants and thereby complete the five temples.

sentences.zh: 又延業、盧觀前經詳議，並據許慎、鄭玄之解，謂天子、諸侯作主，大夫及士則無。

translations.literal: Moreover, Yanye and Lu Guan in their earlier detailed deliberations both relied on the explanations of Xu Shen and Zheng Xuan, holding that the Son of Heaven and feudal lords establish tablet-lords, while grandees and common officers do not.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in their earlier detailed deliberations Yanye and Lu Guan both relied on Xu Shen and Zheng Xuan, holding that the Son of Heaven and feudal lords establish tablet-lords, while grandees and common officers do not.

sentences.zh: 意謂此議雖出前儒之事，實未允情禮。

translations.literal: I deem that although this proposal comes from former Ruists, it truly does not accord with sentiment and ritual.
translations.idiomatic: I deem that although this view comes from former Ruists, it truly does not accord with sentiment and ritual.

sentences.zh: 何以言之？

translations.literal: How is this to be explained?
translations.idiomatic: How is this to be explained?

sentences.zh: 原夫作主之禮，本以依神，孝子之心，非主莫依。

translations.literal: Tracing the origin, the rite of making tablet-lords is fundamentally to rely on the spirit; the filial son's heart has nothing to rely on if not the tablet-lord.
translations.idiomatic: At root, the rite of making tablet-lords exists to give the spirit a dwelling; in a filial son's heart, nothing else can lodge the spirit.

sentences.zh: 今銘旌紀柩，設重憑神，祭必有尸，神必有廟，皆所以展事孝敬，想象平存。

translations.literal: Now inscribed banners record the coffin, the soul-seat is set to lodge the spirit, sacrifice must have a personator, the spirit must have a temple—all are means to extend the performance of reverence and filial piety, imagining the deceased as still living.
translations.idiomatic: Banners inscribe the coffin, the soul-seat lodges the spirit, sacrifice requires a personator, and the spirit requires a temple—all extend reverent service and filial duty, imagining the dead as though still alive.

sentences.zh: 上自天子，下逮於士，如此四事，並同其禮。

translations.literal: From the Son of Heaven down to the common officer, in these four matters the ritual is the same.
translations.idiomatic: From the Son of Heaven down to the common officer, in these four matters the ritual is the same.

sentences.zh: 何至於主，惟謂王侯。

translations.literal: Why, when it comes to tablet-lords, is it said to apply only to kings and marquises?
translations.idiomatic: Why, when it comes to tablet-lords alone, is it said to apply only to kings and marquises?

sentences.zh: 禮云：「重，主道也。」

translations.literal: The Rites say: "The soul-seat is the way of the tablet-lord."
translations.idiomatic: The Rites say: "The soul-seat is the way of the tablet-lord."

sentences.zh: 此為埋重則立主矣。

translations.literal: This is because when the soul-seat is buried one then establishes a tablet-lord.
translations.idiomatic: This is because when the soul-seat is buried one then establishes a tablet-lord.

sentences.zh: 故王肅曰：「重，未立主之禮也。」

translations.literal: Therefore Wang Su said: "The soul-seat is the rite before the tablet-lord is established."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Wang Su said: "The soul-seat is the rite before the tablet-lord is established."

sentences.zh: 士喪禮亦設重，則士有主明矣。

translations.literal: The Common Officer Mourning Rites also set up a soul-seat; thus the common officer has a tablet-lord—this is clear.
translations.idiomatic: The Common Officer Mourning Rites also set up a soul-seat; thus the common officer has a tablet-lord—this is clear.

sentences.zh: 孔悝反祏，載之左史；

translations.literal: When Kong Kui returned the spirit tablet, it was recorded in the Zuo Tradition;
translations.idiomatic: When Kong Kui returned the spirit tablet, it was recorded in the Zuo Tradition;

sentences.zh: 饋食設主，著於逸禮。

translations.literal: setting out food and establishing a tablet-lord is set forth in the Lost Rites.
translations.idiomatic: presenting food and establishing a tablet-lord is set forth in the Lost Rites.

sentences.zh: 大夫及士，既得有廟題紀祖考，何可無主。

translations.literal: If grandees and common officers may have temple inscriptions recording ancestors and fathers, how can they lack tablet-lords?
translations.idiomatic: If grandees and common officers may have temple inscriptions recording ancestors and fathers, how can they lack tablet-lords?

sentences.zh: 公羊傳：「君有事于廟，聞大夫之喪，去樂卒事；

translations.literal: The Gongyang Commentary: "When the ruler has business at the temple and hears of a grandee's mourning, he removes music and finishes the affair;
translations.idiomatic: The Gongyang Commentary: "When the ruler has business at the temple and hears of a grandee's mourning, he removes music and finishes the affair;

sentences.zh: 大夫聞君之喪，攝主而往。」

translations.literal: when a grandee hears of the ruler's mourning, he takes the acting tablet-lord and goes."
translations.idiomatic: when a grandee hears of the ruler's mourning, he takes the acting tablet-lord and goes."

sentences.zh: 今以為攝主者，攝神斂主而已，不暇待徹祭也。

translations.literal: Now those who take this to mean "acting tablet-lord" mean one who gathers in the spirit and receives the tablet-lord—there is no leisure to await the concluding sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Now those who take this to mean "acting tablet-lord" mean one who gathers in the spirit and receives the tablet-lord—there is no leisure to await the concluding sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 何休云：「宗人攝行主事而往也。」

translations.literal: He Xiu said: "The lineage officer acts in place of the tablet-lord and goes."
translations.idiomatic: He Xiu said: "The lineage officer acts in place of the tablet-lord and goes."

sentences.zh: 意謂不然。

translations.literal: I deem this is not so.
translations.idiomatic: I deem this is not so.

sentences.zh: 君聞臣喪，尚為之不懌，況臣聞君喪，豈得安然代主終祭也。

translations.literal: When the ruler hears of a minister's mourning, he is still displeased by it; how much more when a minister hears of the ruler's mourning—how could he calmly replace the tablet-lord and complete the sacrifice?
translations.idiomatic: If even when the ruler hears of a minister's mourning he is displeased, how much less could a minister, hearing of the ruler's mourning, calmly stand in for the tablet-lord and finish the sacrifice?

sentences.zh: 又相國立廟，設主依神，主無貴賤，紀座而已。

translations.literal: Moreover, when the Chancellor establishes a temple and sets up tablet-lords to lodge the spirits, tablet-lords have no distinction of noble or base—they merely record the seat.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when the Chancellor establishes a temple and sets up tablet-lords to lodge the spirits, tablet-lords have no distinction of noble or base—they merely record the seat.

sentences.zh: 若位擬諸侯者，則有主，位為大夫者，則無主。

translations.literal: If one whose rank matches feudal lords then has a tablet-lord, while one whose rank is grandee then has none,
translations.idiomatic: If one whose rank matches feudal lords then has a tablet-lord, while one whose rank is grandee then has none,

sentences.zh: 便是三神有主，一位獨闕，求諸情禮，實所未安。

translations.literal: then of the three spirits two have tablet-lords while one seat alone is vacant—seeking this in sentiment and ritual, it truly is not settled.
translations.idiomatic: then of the three spirits two have tablet-lords while one seat alone is vacant—sought in sentiment and ritual, this truly is not settled.

sentences.zh: 宜通為主，以銘神位。

translations.literal: One should universally make tablet-lords to inscribe the spirit seats.
translations.idiomatic: Tablet-lords should be made universally to inscribe the spirit seats.

sentences.zh: 懌又議曰：「古者七廟，廟堂皆別。

translations.literal: Yi also argued: "In antiquity the seven temples each had separate halls.
translations.idiomatic: Yi also argued: "In antiquity the seven temples each had separate halls.

sentences.zh: 光武已來，異室同堂。

translations.literal: Since Emperor Guangwu, different chambers share one hall.
translations.idiomatic: Since Emperor Guangwu, separate chambers have been housed in a single hall.

sentences.zh: 故先朝祀堂令云：『廟皆四栿五架，北廂設坐，東昭西穆。』

translations.literal: Therefore the former court's temple-sacrifice ordinance said: "Temples are all four purlins and five bays; the north wing sets seats, zhao in the east and mu in the west."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the former court's temple-sacrifice ordinance said: "Temples are all four purlins and five bays; the north wing sets seats, zhao in the east and mu in the west."

sentences.zh: 是以相國構廟，唯制一室，同祭祖考。

translations.literal: Therefore when the Chancellor constructed a temple, he made only one chamber, jointly sacrificing to ancestors and fathers.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore when the Chancellor constructed a temple, he made only one chamber, jointly sacrificing to ancestors and fathers.

sentences.zh: 比來諸王立廟者，自任私造，不依公令，或五或一，參差無準。

translations.literal: Princes who in recent times have established temples have done so on private authority, not following the public ordinance—some five, some one, uneven and without standard.
translations.idiomatic: Princes who in recent times have established temples have done so on private authority, not following the public ordinance—some five chambers, some one, uneven and without standard.

sentences.zh: 要須議行新令，然後定其法制。

translations.literal: It is essential first to deliberate and enact a new ordinance, and only then fix the institutional form.
translations.idiomatic: It is essential first to deliberate and enact a new ordinance, and only then fix the institutional form.

sentences.zh: 相國之廟，已造一室，實合朝令。

translations.literal: The Chancellor's temple has already built one chamber, which truly accords with the court ordinance.
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellor's temple has already built one chamber, which truly accords with the court ordinance.

sentences.zh: 宜即依此，展其享祀。」

translations.literal: One should at once follow this and extend its offerings."
translations.idiomatic: It should at once follow this and extend its offerings."

sentences.zh: 詔依懌議。

translations.literal: An edict followed Yi's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed Yi's proposal.

sentences.zh: 天平四年四月，七帝神主既遷於太廟，太社石主將遷於社宮。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year of Tianping, the spirit tablets of the seven emperors having already been moved to the Grand Temple, the stone tablet-lord of the Grand Altars of Soil and Grain was about to be moved to the Altars Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fourth year of Tianping, once the spirit tablets of the seven emperors had been transferred to the Grand Temple, the stone tablet-lord of the Grand Altars of Soil and Grain was to be moved to the Altars Palace.

sentences.zh: 禮官云應用幣。

translations.literal: The ritual officers said silks should be used.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officers said silks should be used.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎裴伯茂時為祖祀文，伯茂據故事，太和中遷社宮，高祖用牲不用幣，遂以奏聞。

translations.literal: Palace Secretariat Gentleman Pei Bomo was at the time drafting the ancestral-sacrifice text; Bomo, relying on precedent, noted that in the Taihe era when the Altars Palace was moved, Emperor Gaozu used victims and not silks, and so submitted a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Secretariat Gentleman Pei Bomo was at the time drafting the ancestral-sacrifice text; Bomo, relying on precedent, noted that in the Taihe era when the Altars Palace was moved, Emperor Gaozu used victims and not silks, and so submitted a memorial.

sentences.zh: 于時議者或引大戴禮，遷廟用幣，今遷社宜不殊。

translations.literal: At the time some in the deliberation cited the Elder Dai's Rites: moving temples uses silks; moving the altars now should not differ.
translations.idiomatic: At the time some in the deliberation cited the Elder Dai's Rites: moving temples uses silks; moving the altars now should not differ.

sentences.zh: 伯茂據尚書召誥，應用牲。

translations.literal: Bomo relied on the Announcement of the Duke of Shao in the Documents, holding that victims should be used.
translations.idiomatic: Bomo relied on the Announcement of the Duke of Shao in the Documents, holding that victims should be used.

sentences.zh: 詔遂從之。

translations.literal: An edict thereupon followed this.
translations.idiomatic: An edict thereupon followed this.

sentences.zh: 武定六年二月，將營齊獻武王廟，議定室數、形制。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixth year of Wuding, when about to build the temple of Prince Xianwu of Qi, they deliberated fixing the number of chambers and the form.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the sixth year of Wuding, when about to build the temple of Prince Xianwu of Qi, they deliberated fixing the number of chambers and the form.

translations.literal: Concurrently Minister of Revenue Cui Ang, Director of the Directorate of Agriculture Lu Yuanming, Director of the Palace Library Wang Yuanjing, Regular Attendant Pei Xianbo, Chancellor of the Directorate of Education Li Hun, Censor-in-Chief Lu Cao, Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Li Qian, Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat Yang Xiuzhi, former Governor of Southern Qing Province Zheng Boyou, Secretariat Assistant Cui Jie, Erudite of the Directorate of Education Xing Zhi, Erudite of the Directorate of Education Zong Huizhen, Erudite of the Imperial Academy Zhang Yu, Erudite of the Imperial Academy Gao Yuanshou, Assistant Instructor of the Directorate of Education Wang Xianji, and others argued: "Investigating the Rites, feudal lords have five temples—the Grand Ancestor and four temples of kin.

sentences.zh: 今獻武王始封之君，便是太祖，既通親廟，不容立五室。

translations.literal: Now Prince Xianwu is the first enfeoffed lord and is therefore the Grand Ancestor; since kin temples are already included, one cannot establish five chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Now Prince Xianwu is the first enfeoffed lord and is therefore the Grand Ancestor; since kin temples are already included, one cannot establish five chambers.

sentences.zh: 且帝王親廟，亦不過四。

translations.literal: Moreover, even for emperors and kings, temples of kin do not exceed four.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, even for emperors and kings, temples of kin do not exceed four.

sentences.zh: 今宜四室二間，兩頭各一頰室，夏頭徘徊鵄尾。

translations.literal: Now there should be four chambers in two bays, one flank chamber at each end, with summer-eave pacing and owl-tail finials.
translations.idiomatic: Now there should be four chambers in two bays, one flank chamber at each end, with summer-eave pacing and owl-tail finials.

sentences.zh: 又案禮圖，諸侯止開南門，而二王後祔祭儀法，執事列於廟東門之外。

translations.literal: Moreover, investigating the Ritual Diagrams, feudal lords open only the south gate; yet in the rites for collateral sacrifice by the two royal successors, the officiants are arrayed outside the temple's east gate.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, investigating the Ritual Diagrams, feudal lords open only the south gate; yet in the rites for collateral sacrifice by the two royal successors, the officiants are arrayed outside the temple's east gate.

sentences.zh: 既有東門，明非一門。

translations.literal: Since there is an east gate, it is clear there is not only one gate.
translations.idiomatic: Since there is an east gate, it is clear there is not only one gate.

sentences.zh: 獻武禮數既隆，備物殊等。

translations.literal: Prince Xianwu's ritual standing is already lofty, and his equipped objects are of special rank.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xianwu's ritual standing is already lofty, and his equipped objects are of special rank.

sentences.zh: 準據今廟，宜開四門。

translations.literal: According to the present temple, four gates should be opened.
translations.idiomatic: According to the present temple, four gates should be opened.

sentences.zh: 內院南面開三門，餘面及外院，四面皆一門。

translations.literal: The inner court's south face should open three gates; the remaining faces and the outer court should each have one gate on all four sides.
translations.idiomatic: The inner court's south face should open three gates; the remaining faces and the outer court should each have one gate on all four sides.

sentences.zh: 其內院牆，四面皆架為步廊。

translations.literal: The inner court's walls on all four sides should be bridged as pacing galleries.
translations.idiomatic: The inner court's walls on all four sides should be bridged as pacing galleries.

sentences.zh: 南出夾門，各置一屋，以置禮器及祭服。

translations.literal: South of the flanking gates, one building should be set on each side to store ritual vessels and sacrificial garments.
translations.idiomatic: South of the flanking gates, one building should be set on each side to store ritual vessels and sacrificial garments.

sentences.zh: 內外門牆，並用赭堊。

translations.literal: Inner and outer gates and walls should all use ochre plaster.
translations.idiomatic: Inner and outer gates and walls should all use ochre plaster.

sentences.zh: 廟東門道南置齋坊；

translations.literal: South of the temple's east gate road, a fasting lodge should be set;
translations.idiomatic: South of the temple's east gate road, a fasting lodge should be set;

sentences.zh: 道北置二坊，西為典祠廨并厨宰，東為廟長廨并置車輅；

translations.literal: north of the road two lodges should be set: west for the temple-officiant office and kitchen, east for the temple warden's office and for setting out chariots;
translations.idiomatic: north of the road two lodges should be set: west for the temple-officiant office and kitchen, east for the temple warden's office and for setting out chariots;

sentences.zh: 漢書卷三０藝文志：「禮古經者出於魯淹中及孔氏。」

translations.literal: Hanshu, juan 30, "Bibliographic Treatise": "The ancient classic of Ritual came forth from Yanzhong of Lu and the Kong clan."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Han, juan 30, "Bibliographic Treatise": "The ancient classic of Ritual came forth from Yanzhong of Lu and the Kong clan."

sentences.zh: 魏明帝以景初三年正月崩至五年正月積二十五晦為大祥 通典卷五０禘祫下載孫惠蔚議「五年」作「廢帝正始二年」。

translations.literal: On "Emperor Ming of Wei died in the first month of the third year of Jingchu; by the first month of the fifth year, twenty-five last days of the month had accumulated for the great auspicious end of mourning" — Tongdian, juan 50, "Di and Xia," records Sun Huiwei's proposal with "five years" reading "the second year of Zhengshi under the Deposed Emperor."
translations.idiomatic: On the passage about Emperor Ming of Wei's mourning: Tongdian, juan 50, "Di and Xia," records Sun Huiwei's proposal with "five years" reading "the second year of Zhengshi under the Deposed Emperor."

sentences.zh: 按景初止三年，明年曹芳

translations.literal: Comment: Jingchu lasted only three years; the next year Cao Fang
translations.idiomatic: Comment: The Jingchu era lasted only three years; the next year Cao Fang

translations.literal: 〈the Deposed Emperor〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈the Deposed Emperor〉

translations.literal: changed the era name to Zhengshi; in the first month of the second year of Zhengshi it was exactly twenty-five last days of the month.
translations.idiomatic: changed the era name to Zhengshi; in the first month of the second year of Zhengshi it was exactly twenty-five last days of the month.

translations.idiomatic: The character "five" is suspected to be a corruption of "correct," with the two characters "shi er" omitted below.

sentences.zh: 升食太祖 諸本「升」訛「外」，不可通，今據通典卷五０改。

translations.idiomatic: On "ascend to share food at the Grand Ancestor": in all editions "ascend" is corrupt as "outside," which will not parse; it is now emended according to Tongdian, juan 50.

sentences.zh: 宜待三年終乃後祫禘 諸本無「三」字，通典卷五０載崔亮議有。

translations.idiomatic: On "one should wait until the three years are ended and only then perform di and ti": all editions lack the character "three"; Tongdian, juan 50, records Cui Liang's proposal with it.

translations.idiomatic: Comment: If it read "at year's end,"

translations.literal: from Emperor Xiaowen's death it would be less than two years—this would not accord with the ritual systems of successive ages that speak of "di only after three years"; how could one say "following ancient ritual and the deliberations of Jin and Wei, together with the Jingming precedent"?
translations.idiomatic: From Emperor Wen's death it would be less than two years—this would not accord with successive ritual systems that speak of di only after three years; how could one say "following ancient ritual and the deliberations of Jin and Wei, together with the Jingming precedent"?

translations.literal: Thus one knows that "three" should be supplied above "year"; it is now supplied on this authority.
translations.idiomatic: Thus one knows that "three" should be supplied above "year"; it is now supplied on this authority.

translations.idiomatic: On "Zheng Xuan's commentary says": in all editions "says" reads "great"; Cefu yuanguan, juan 582

translations.idiomatic: 〈page 6977〉

sentences.zh: 作「云」。

translations.literal: reads "says."
translations.idiomatic: reads "says."

translations.literal: Comment: If it read "great," it would have to be read continuously with "ti and suburban" below; yet Zheng Xuan's original commentary on the "Methods of Sacrifice" in the Book of Rites has no character "great," and it is also redundant in meaning—thus one knows it is a corruption of "says," and it is now emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 實四廟言五者容顯考為始封君子故也 冊府卷五八二

translations.literal: On "speaking of five temples when there are in fact four" — it accommodates the case where the illustrious forefather is the first enfeoffed lord — Cefu yuanguan, juan 582
translations.idiomatic: On the phrase "speaking of five temples when there are in fact four": it accommodates the case where the illustrious forefather is the first enfeoffed lord — Cefu yuanguan, juan 582

sentences.zh: 此句作「實四廟孫而言五廟者，容顯考為始封子也」，與今本禮記文王世子合。

translations.literal: This sentence reads: "When speaking of five temples though there are in fact four-temple descendants, it accommodates the illustrious forefather as the first enfeoffed son" — which agrees with the present edition of the "Heir of King Wen" chapter in the Book of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: This sentence reads: "When speaking of five temples though there are in fact four-temple descendants, it accommodates the illustrious forefather as the first enfeoffed son" — which agrees with the present edition of the "Heir of King Wen" chapter in the Book of Rites.

sentences.zh: 然觀下文李琰之議引鄭注與此同，或當時禮記自有別本與今傳本不同，非必脫誤，冊府當據今傳本改。

translations.literal: Yet observing Li Yanzhi's discussion below, which cites Master Zheng's commentary in the same way, perhaps the Book of Rites at that time had a separate edition differing from the present transmitted text — not necessarily an omission or error; Cefu yuanguan should have emended according to the present transmitted text.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄云實四廟而言五廟者容高祖為始封君之子 按此引鄭注亦與今傳本不同

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan says: "When speaking of five temples though there are in fact four, it accommodates the high ancestor as the son of the first enfeoffed lord." Comment: this citation of Master Zheng also differs from the present transmitted text.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan says: "When speaking of five temples though there are in fact four, it accommodates the high ancestor as the son of the first enfeoffed lord." Comment: this citation of Master Zheng also differs from the present transmitted text.

translations.idiomatic: 〈See the entry above.〉

translations.literal: Below "four temples" there is no character "grandson"; below "first enfeoffment" there is the character "lord" — both agreeing with the Zheng commentary cited above by Wang Siqi, Li Yanzhi, and Yuan Ji's request to participate in sacrifice; yet in the transmitted Book of Rites and in the Wang and Li discussions "high ancestor" all read "illustrious forefather."

sentences.zh: 原文當作「顯考」，而「顯考廟」即「高祖廟」，當是王延業以意改易，今不改。

translations.literal: The original text should read "illustrious forefather," and the "illustrious forefather temple" is the "high ancestor temple" — this was likely Wang Yanye's intentional alteration; it is not changed now.
translations.idiomatic: The original text should read "illustrious forefather," and the illustrious forefather temple is the high ancestor temple — this was likely Wang Yanye's intentional alteration; it is not changed now.

translations.literal: Comment: the Ritual Apocrypha speaks of five temples — the founding-ancestor temple plus one and four kin temples make five; without the three characters "founding ancestor one," there would be only four kin temples — how could one speak of five temples? Thus one knows text is missing.

translations.literal: Further, "clarifying the first enfeoffed lord" and so on are Lu Guan's explanation of the Ritual Apocrypha language; without the character "clarifying," the original Ritual Apocrypha text and Lu Guan's words would be confused.

translations.idiomatic: All are now supplied on this authority.
